INTRODUCTION 
 
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture, having been authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do 
hereby present this Three Hundred Sixth Report on Action Taken by the Government on the 
Recommendations/ Observations of the Committee contained in its Two Hundred and Ninety 
Fifth Report on the subject ‘Potential of Tourist Spots in the country - Connectivity and 
Outreach’. 
2. The Two Hundred and Ninety Fifth Report of the Department -related Parliamentary 
Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented on the  27th July, 2021 
to the Parliament. 
3.  The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its 
Two Hundred and Ninety Fifth Report were received from the Ministry of Tourism on 21st 
December, 2021. 
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the  31st 
January, 2022.   
 
 
(T.G. Venkatesh)

recommendations/observations as contained in its Two Hundred Ninety Fifth Report on 
Potential for Tourist Spots in the country – Connectivity and Outreach of the Ministry of 
Tourism which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 27th July 2021.

been categorized as follows:-

2 
 
 
CHAPTER I  
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
 
PROGRESS REPORT 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
1 The Committee also notes that availability of land free from all encumbrances is the 
responsibility of the respective State Governments/ Union Territories. The Committee would 
like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard.  
(Para 11) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
1.1 Providing the land free from all encumbrances is the responsibility of the State 
Governments/ Union Territory Administrations. As per the draft guidelines of the Swadesh 
Darshan 2.0, land is a non -admissible component and will not be funded under the Swade sh 
Darshan scheme of the Ministry. The Ministry of Tourism (MoT) further vide OM no. SD-
8/10/2020 dated 11.6.2021 has issued the format for „Physical Completion Certificate‟ 
which is to be submitted by Head of the Implementing Agency and Administrative Sec retary. 
Vide this certificate state has to undertake that the facility and the land on which the project 
has been executed will not be transferred/ sold / alienated in any matter whatsoever without 
the written consent and prior approval of the MoT, Government of India and facilities created 
shall be used only for tourism purposes.  
 
1.2 Under the Scheme Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure 
Development, Central Agencies which are the recipient of the financial assistance are 
responsible for making the land available for development & other allied facilities related to 
execution of the project.  
 

3 
 
1.3 Providing the land, free from any kind of encumbrances, is the responsibility of the 
State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations. In t erms of the guidelines of 
PRASHAD Scheme land is an inadmissible item under the scheme and hence, no funds are 
released for the purpose of acquisition of the land for the project.  
1.4 To address the issue of unavailability of land parcels for the approved  works under 
PRASHAD Scheme, as per the check -list for preparation of DPRs for the project under 
PRASHAD Scheme it has been made obligatory on part of the State Government to provide a 
land availability certificate duly signed by an officer of the level of  at least Secretary of 
Tourism Department of the State / UT concerned. In addition, the interventions for which 
land availability is not confirmed by the respective State Government / UT Administration 
are not being approved under the projects in the Scheme.  
 
1.5 Moreover, under PRASHAD Scheme first installment is released only for those 
interventions for which works have been awarded after completion of tendering process by 
the State/UT.  
In addition, further releases are done only for those interventions on which physical execution 
is in progress. To calculate the amount of second or further releases, the costs of works for 
which tender have not been completed or without any physical progress, are not accounted 
for.  
 
 
STALLED PROJECTS 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
2. The Committee notes that for all the projects that have been sanctioned since the year 
2017, only 50 percent of the sanctioned amount was released so far. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends the Ministry to adopt strategies for speedy completion of the stalled 
projects. The Committee is of the view that this will also help in effective utilization of funds 
and skilled manpower to the maximum possible extent. 
(Para 28) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 

4 
 
2.1 Under the scheme Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure 
Development, funds are released to the Central Agency/ implementing agency in three 
instalments as per following details: 
As regards project taken up by IDD of the Ministry under the scheme Assistance to Central 
Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development, funds are released to the Central Agency/ 
implementing agency in three instalments as per following details: 
 
 
1. First instalment – 50% of the Central Financial Assistance amount at the time of 
sanction  
2. Second instalment - 30% of the sanctioned amount on submission of Utilization 
Certificate of the first instalment  
3. Third instalment- 20% of the sanctioned amount on submission of final Utilization 
Certificate by the implementing agency after the entire work  is completed along 
with an affidavit for Management of Assets created and an undertaking for 
maintenance of the same as per applicable GFR. 
 
2.2 The second instalment is released only after receipt of Utilisation Certificate of the 
first instalment. Continued efforts are being made for timely submission of UCs 
2.3 The second instalment is released only after receipt of Utilisation Certificate of the 
first instalment. Continued efforts are being made for timely submission of UCs. 
2.4 Now Ministry is also se tting up IT based monitoring portals for even closer progress 
of the projects. 
2.5 As far as PRASHAD Scheme is concerned, in addition to rigours follow -ups at the 
Division level, timely review done at the Joint Secretary levels with respect to the pending 
Utilizations Certificates.   It may kindly be appreciated that under PRASHAD Scheme the 
only pending UC amount to Rs. 10 Cr. for the fund released for the project “Infrastructure 
Development at Puri, Shree Jagannath Dham – Ramachandi - Prachi River front at  Deuli 
under Mega Circuit”.    Efforts are being put at the top levels of the MOT to neutralize this 
pending Utilization Certificate also. 
 
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 

5 
 
 
3 The Committee recommends that an audit of the expenditure incurred under the 
Scheme of 'Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development' should 
also be conducted, the details of which should be uploaded on a web based platform for 
effective monitoring of the progress of the implementation. 
 (Para 29) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
3.1 The expenditure of the Ministry is audited by the designated audited officer (Internal 
as well as Statuary audits) . Further, the Ministry has got engaged third party (Quality 
Council of India) for evaluation of  the projects undertaken by it. 
3.2  Internal audit is conducted from time to time. 
3.3 All the projects undertaken with Ministry of Railways under the joint development of 
creation of amenities and facilities at the identified railway stations are being evaluated by 
QCI. 
 
 
 
INTEGRATED TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
4. The Committee observes that the tourism sector not only provides employment to wide 
spectrum of job seekers from the unskilled to the specialized but also makes significant 
contribution to the national e conomy by stimulating other economic factors through its 
backward and forward linkages. Since tourism is multi -sectoral activity and the related 
sector includes airlines, surface transport, hotels, basic infrastructure, etc, the growth of the 
sector cannot  be attained unless issues related to all these sectors are addressed 
simultaneously. The Committee notes from the information furnished by the Ministry that 
with a view to make India a 5 trillion dollar economy by 2024 -25, the SGoS Tourism Sector 
Plan aims at implementation of 21 tourism development projects over the next five years. The 
Committee is of the considered view that if the goal of becoming a 5 trillion dollar economy 
is to be achieved, the Government needs to fastrack the development of these 2 1 tourism 

6 
 
infrastructure projects in collaboration with all the Ministries/ entities concerned. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that convergence and synergy be created across 
programmes of Ministries/ Departments so that the implementation of these 21  tourism 
development projects could be expedited and an integrated development of enabling 
infrastructure through partnerships with all the stakeholders could be accomplished. The 
Committee desires to be kept apprised of the strategies adopted in this regard. 
(Para 31) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
4.1 Ministry of Tourism works in close collaboration with Central Ministries/State 
Governments/various Stakeholders for the development of tourism in the country. Different 
mechanisms and strategies to seek synergy and  convergence with stakeholders for integrated 
development of enabling tourism infrastructure are: 
 
i. National & Regional Conference of State Tourism Ministers are held to discuss 
various issues related to the development of tourism sector in the country. 
ii. National Tourism Advisory Council serves as a ‘Think Tank’ of experts in the field 
of tourism and advises the Ministry on various tourism related issues. It includes 
representatives of various Union Ministries, Trade and Industry Associations and 
Individual Experts in the field of travel and tourism management.  
iii. The Inter -Ministerial Coordination Committee on Tourism Sector (IMCCTS) 
facilitates resolution of Inter -Ministerial issues involved in the development of 
tourism in the country.  
iv. A Task Force has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Secretary (Tourism), 
Govt. of India to address various issues related to tourism as per the 
recommendations of the Sectoral Groups of Secretaries (SGoS) for Tourism 
Sectoral Plan. The Task Force comprises representativ es from the Ministries of 
Civil Aviation, External Affairs, Home Affairs, Railways, Road T ransport & 
Highways, Culture, DoNER, Environment & Forests and IRCTC, ASI. 
 
4.2 Meetings/Consultations are held from time to time with various stakeholders to 
take suggestions/inputs for the development and promotion of tourism sector in the country. 
 

7 
 
i. The last National Conference of Tourism Ministers was held at Ashok Hotel, New 
Delhi in August 2019. The conference was attended by around 20 State Tourism 
Ministers and Senior Officers from State and Central Ministries. In the above meeting 
various issues such as Development of Adventure Tourism, Status of projects 
sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan & PRASHAD Schemes, Bed & 
Breakfast/Homestay Scheme Guidelines as well as be st practices in tourism sector 
and social media campaigns undertaken by the selected State Governments were 
discussed.  
ii. Ministry of Tourism (MoT) organized Regional Tourism & Culture Ministers 
Conference of the North Eastern States on 9th & 10th September 2021at Guwahati, 
Assam to discuss development of tourism and connectivity related issues in the North 
Eastern Region. The North East State Tourism Ministers Conference featured 
presentations by M/o Tourism, M/o DoNER, M/o Civil Aviation, M/o Road Transport 
& Highways and M/o Railways to apprise the participants about the various projects 
and initiatives being taken by the Central Government for the development of North 
Eastern Region. Technical sessions were held to review the progress of the various 
projects sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD Schemes as well as to 
have discussions on adventure tourism and promotion & marketing. 
iii. MoT organised Regional Tourism and Culture Ministers Conference of the Southern 
Region on 28th & 29th October 2021 in Ben galuru, Karnataka to apprise the 
participants about the various projects and initiatives being taken by the Central 
Government for the development of the tourism in the region. 
iv. The last NTAC was constituted on 27th October, 2016 with the validity of 3 years and 
its tenure ended on 26th October, 2019. Two meetings of NTAC were conducted on 
12.04.2018 and 21 -22 Feb. 2019 at Hotel Samrat, New Delhi and Statue of Unity, 
Kevadiya, Gujarat respectively. The 3rd and last meeting of the NTAC was held on 
04.10.2019 at Paryatan Parv, VIP Lounge, Rajpath Lawns, New Delhi. Several 
suggestions had been raised during the brainstorming discussion on which MoT is 
taking necessary action in close collaboration with Central Ministries/ State 
Governments /various Stakeholders for the development of tourism in the country. 
v. MoT has taken up several issues through the mechanism of IMCCTS. Rationalization 
of e-visa fee, guide license matters, haulage charge on tourist trains, etc. have been 
resolved through the meetings of IMCCTS. 

8 
 
vi. A Task Force has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Secretary (Tourism), 
which includes representative of several Ministries/ Departments. The first meeting of 
the Task Force was held on 1st September 2020. It was followed up with Virtual 
meeting with the representative of the said Committee in October, 2020.  
4.3 The Task Force headed by Secretary (Tourism) has enabled the MoT to work closely 
with Ministry of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Ministry of 
Railways for the purpos e of enhancing connectivity to tourist destinations. The matter 
regarding monitoring the implementation of tourism routes under RCS -UDAN has been 
expedited and as a result 29 of the 46 tourism routes taken by the bidders under RCS -UDAN-
3, have been made operational. 
4.4 Similarly, the Ministry has forwarded 50 destinations in the first phase to Ministry of 
Road Transport & Highways for better road connectivity and way side amenities. Out of 
these 50 destinations, 23 of them are in the jurisdiction of MoRTH and rest are with 
concerned State Government/UT Administration or Border Road Organisation. The matter 
has been taken up with the concerned organisations. In the 2nd phase MoT has sent a list of an 
additional 114 destinations to MoRTH for improvement of road connectivity. 
4.5 The issue of connectivity to tourism destinations including Pilgrimage centres have 
been expedited through the meeting. IRCTC has informed that they have already started a 
number of trains dedicated to the tourism theme destinations, i ncluding pilgrimage 
destinations. 
 
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
5 The Committee recommends that the Ministry should also ensure that these projects 
are completed within the designated timeline and the approved cost so that proper air 
connectivity is established between the less connected regions with high tourism potential at 
affordable prices which would provide a boost to tourism industry leading to higher 
employment and greater revenues. 
(Para 34) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 

9 
 
5.1 The Ministry of Civil A viation (MoCA) has constituted a M onitoring -cum-
Coordination Committee under RCS UDAN Scheme in which Ministry of Tourism has also 
been co-opted as the member. Meeting of the Committee is held regularly in order to monitor 
and evaluate the status of the projects.  
5.2 The Monitoring Committee formed by MoCA has met on the following dates during 
the financial year 2020 -21 and 2021 -22to review and monitor the work to be carried out in 
RCS-UDAN:- 08.06.2020, 06.07.2020, 13.08.2020, 14.12.2020, 08.04.2021, 16.10.2021. 
5.3 29 out of the 46 tourism routes have already been made operational. 
Ministry of Civil Aviation has already launched RCS -UDAN-4, under which priority has 
been given to connect the destinations located in North Eastern region of the country. 
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
6.  The Committee observes that despite India being endowed with nature's bounty and 
being a land of great tourism potential, its share in International Tourist Arrivals is a meager 
1.23% (Source- India Tourism Statistics at a Glance 2020). Poor connectivity, especially air 
connectivity remains one of the biggest hurdles and is impacting the growth of the Indian 
tourism sector in general and that of International Tourist Arrivals in particular. The issue 
related to connectivity was deliberated with the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 01 -09-2020 
wherein details pertaining to development of 100 airports and 78 routes approved under the 
fourth round of Regional Connectivity Scheme were inter -alia shared. Since the all round 
department of the tourism sector bas the potential to act as the key driver of inclusive growth 
and unless air connectivity improves, the number of high -end tourists is not going to 
increase, the Committee recommends that at least 19 Iconic spots should be taken on priority 
and suitable mechanism be developed to get the above projects implemented within a 
designated time-frame.  
(Para 40) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1 Development of Iconic Tourist Destination‟ is not yet approved.  
6.2 Under RCS UDAN -3, The Ministry of Tourism, in consultation with stakeholders 
had forwarded a list of important tourist destinations, to the Ministry of Civil Aviation. Out 
of these 46 routes, 29 routes are operationalized and 8 of them (Dibrugarh to Dimapu r/ 

10 
 
Dimapur to Dibrugarh/ Dimapur to Imphal/ Imphal to Dimapur/Agartala to Aizawl /Aizawl 
to Agartala/ Dibrugarh to Imphal/ Imphal to Dibrugarh) are in the North-East Region.  
 
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
7. The Committee observes that the availability o f hotel rooms in India is limited 
because of acute shortage of land in cities due to land market distortions and there is a need 
to significantly augment hotel room capacity. In order to meet the requirement of 
accommodation, the Committee recommends that the surplus railway land at railway stations 
may be utilized for constructing budget hotels.  
(Para 42) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
7.1 Construction and operation of hotels is primarily a private sector activity. The 
Ministry has been request the Ministry of Railways to consider allotting railway land for 
constructing budget hotels.  
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
8. The Committee desires that this mode of transport facility should be affordable to the 
tourists who could not afford cruise tourism facilities so that cruise tourism can reach the 
masses.  
(Para 49) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
8.1  Ministry during the meeting of “Cruise Tourism Task Force” will take up the matter 
with State Governments.  
8.2 Development of places of tourist interest including cruise terminals, which are under 
the control of Central Agencies are granted financial assi stance under the scheme Assistance 

11 
 
to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development. The focus under the scheme is 
on the improvement / up-gradation of existing products and developing new tourism products 
to the World Standard.  
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
9. The Committee desires the Ministry of Tourism to target foreign tourists, Indians 
living abroad, foreign universities etc. digitally to market the country's brand image as one of 
the popular tourist destinations globally and develop specia l travel packages covering three 
to four prominent destinations of every region in the country.  
(Para 55) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
9.1 Ministry of Tourism (MoT) actively markets country’s tourist destinations through 
digital mediums under its promotional campaign including Global Media Campaigns.  
9.2 The MoT, through India Tourism Offices Overseas endeavors to position India as a 
preferred tourism destination in the tourism generating markets to promote various tourism 
products, destinations to increase India’s share in the global tourism market.  
9.3 The objectives are met through an integrated marketing and promotional strategy and 
a synergized campaign in association with the Travel Trade, State Governments and Indian 
Missions abroad. Promotional activities are also undertaken on digital platform. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
10. The Committee is of the view that many advertisement agencies often intend to 
increase their revenue by promoting their services, but fail to connect to their target 
audience. The Committee, therefore,• recommends that advertisements should be designed in 
such a way that they connect to their target audience by even reaching to the remotest part of 
the country and by showcasing its rich heritage and culture.  
(Para 59) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 

12 
 
10.1 The Ministry of Tourism (MoT) undertakes publicity & promotio nal activities across 
the country including remotest parts & lesser known destinations through electronic, digital 
& social media. Also, the Domestic offices of the MoT undertake various promotional 
activities on regular basis across the country.  
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
11. The Committee notes that the Scheme of Domestic Promotion and Publicity including 
Market Development Assistance was launched with the major objective of creating a general 
awareness amongst the domestic population about the tourist destinations and to deve lop 
tourist market within the country. The Committee desires that the Ministry should pay 
attention to how people search for traveling options, how they reach out to travelers at the 
right time and in what way they embrace Facebook / Twitter/ Instagram advertisements.  
(Para 60) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
11.1 Ministry through its DPPH scheme is creating awareness about the tourist destinations 
among the citizens of the country. Keeping in line with the ongoin g trends and customer 
behavior, the Ministry is actively using various social media platforms such as Facebook, 
Instagram, and Twitter etc. 
 
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND PUBLICITY 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
12 While appreciating the shift from generic promotion to more focused and niche 
products of the country under the Incredible India 2.0 campaign, the Committee recommends 
that The Ministry should commission surveys for an impact analysis of the campaigns in k ey 
source markets overseas.  
(Para 67) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 

13 
 
12.1 The Ministry of Tourism has a dedicated Media Planning agency which from time to 
time analyze the latest market trends in source markets targeting on the specific products to 
be marketed in that respective markets. Also, it analyzes the impact of the media campaigns.  
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
13 The Committee also recommends that in order to achieve higher international visitor 
levels, country-wise targets of Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) should be worked out and the 
Ministry should focus on diversification of source markets so that countries wh ich offer high 
growth potential but from where present level of tourist is low could be covered.  
(Para 72) 
Reply of the Ministry 
 
13.1 The suggestion of the Committee is noted  
 
 
Recommendation/ Observation

23. The Committee observes that the tourism, travel and hospitality sector which has

pandemic. Though the Government of India has undertaken various fiscal and relief

tourism sector. The Committee notes that as per  the "Report of the Working Group on

create 78 jobs per million rupees of investment compared to 45 jobs in the manufacturing 
sector for similar investment. This critical sector is one of India's large st contributors to

as a catalyst for the recovery of the currently battered economy needs direct Government

3. The Committee takes note of the of the Ministry that the Public Private Partnership

Darshan Scheme and PRASHASD Schemes also have a provision to explore for PPP partner 
for operation, maintenance and sustenance of the facilities created. The Co mmittee observes

services to both domestic and international tourists is a pre -requisite not only to generate 
employment and achieve broad based and inclusive growth of the economy on a sustained 
basis, but also to have a favorable impact on the preservation of art, culture and heritage.

of tourism infrastructure under the SDS and PRASHAD, the Ministry should formu late a 
transparent policy framework for participation of private operators in developing products

CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Committee notes that Highway Safety has been given 35% weightage in NHAI’s 
parameters for assessment and ranking of National Highways. Number of accidents and 
deaths happening on the particular National Highway must be taken into account while 
calculating such scores. 
(Para 21) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1. As per the highway rating criteria for evaluation of Highway Safety scores, 4 marks 
have been allocated to Accidents per km per annum and 4 marks have been allocated to 
Accident Severity Index (fatalities per 100 accidents). 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may take steps to assign scores to all 
the National Highways projects, including the ones executed by State Government PWDs, 
after assessing their quality of construction. A central database may store the scores obtained 
by the different road projects of each concessionaire/contractor, which may be analyzed to 
ascertain the quality of work executed by all the concessionaires. Th e Committee 
recommends that the quality of previous works carried out by the concessionaires should also 
be a factor, besides the bid amount, during the awarding process of a road project tender. 
This would ensure that concessionaires that produce quality roads are not left out of having 
the opportunity to work on a project because of minor differences in bidding amounts. 
(Para 22) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1. Ministry has issued a letter no. RW/NH-33044/15/2021-S&R (P&P) dated 16.04.2021 
regarding Highways Rating Criteria and SOP for undivided carriageway upto 2 -Lane with 
paved shoulders on National Highways. Similarly, NHAI has prepared Highways Rating 
Criteria and SOP for undivided carriageways (four lanes and above) vide its letter 
NHAI/HO/Highways rating/2020 dated 07.07.2020. The rating shall be used to prioritize the 

3 
 
allocation of funds for improving/widening/strengthening different sections of NH on 
different elements of efficiency, safety and user services. The r ating shall also help in 
performance appraisal of deployed contractor/concessionaire/maintaining agency. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
3. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may consider breaking down big road 
projects into smaller chunks so as to attract the interest of the small contractors themselves. 
The Committee feels that provisions should be in place to ensure that there is a well -defined 
lower limit, below which bids for a road project would not be accepted. The Committee 
agrees with the ap prehension raised by the Member of the Committee regarding a likely hit 
on the quality of work that can be carried out by a contractor who bids substantially lower 
than the approved project cost. The Committee believes that such bids are made with the sole  
intent of winning the bid and more often than not, it would not be possible for such bidders to 
do quality work with such low bids. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry 
may lay even greater focus on arriving at accurate estimates for the  project cost for a given 
road project and specify an upper and lower limits within which bids can be placed. 
(Para 25) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1. The Ministry has been able to reduce the overall cost of development of highways 
through increasing competition by right -sizing of construction packages to ensure optimum 
competition during the bidding stage and refinement of eligibility criteria to promot e 
competition. For example, flagship corridors like Delhi Mumbai Expressway and Delhi 
Amritsar Katra Expressway have been segmented into packages of INR ~ 1,000 Cr which has 
made it accessible for upcoming firms. Combined with improvements to the model 
concession agreements the competitiveness of the overall sector has been improved 
significantly.  
3.2. The reduction in average project package sizes (~55 km before FY 17 to ~ 30 km 
currently) led to higher competition - average no. of bids from 5 – 7 in FY 2 0 to 15+ in Q4 
FY 21. This has led to higher discounts competition and increased average discount on EPC 
projects from 7% in FY 20 to 10% in FY 21. 
3.3. The Ministry adheres to the procurement guidelines set by the Ministry of Finance for 
procurement, bidd ing and awarding contracts. The authority is cognizant about such 
aggressive bidding practices by some contractors and has installed checks and balances to 
ensure that project completion is not hindered due to lack of financial resources required for 
the project. One such step is the mandating of the contractors and concessionaires to provide 
additional performance security in cases where significant discounted prices are quoted. 
Recommendation/Observation  

4 
 
4. The Committee recommends that thorough quality checks may be performed before 
the issuance of completion certificate for any NH project, with special focus on rigorous 
testing of quality of the construction material used. The frequency of quality checks 
performed during the construction stage of a proj ect may be increased suitably and 
independent third party audits may be conducted more often in order to deter the connivance 
of the Authority’s Engineer with the road contractors. The Committee further desires that 
extensive quality checks may be performe d when the defect liability period of a project is 
nearing its end, so as to ensure that the issues arising near the end of the defect liability 
period are addressed by the contractor before their liability for the same is over. 
(Para 28) 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1. The quality checks before issue of completion certificate for any NH projects are 
being carried out as specified under Schedule -K of EPC contract and Schedule -I of BOT 
contract. 
 Random quality inspection by engaging retired Senior Govt. officials  are being 
carried out in order to deter the connivance of the Authority’s Engineer with the road 
contractors. 
 During Defect Liability Period, the equipment based monitoring at specified interval 
is being carried out. 
Recommendation/Observation  
5. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should look into the authenticity 
of the quality checks cleared by road projects, which later performed poorly and/or 
deteriorated at a quick pace, since the same alludes to either the insufficiency of the qualit y 
checks in place, or the connivance of the officials/engineers in charge of conducting the 
quality checks. A suitable mechanism may be put in place to ensure that the IRC guidelines 
are followed in the execution of road works without fail. 
(Para 29) 
Reply of the Ministry 
5.1. To ensure that the requisite quality standards are followed during the execution of the 
project and work is carried out as per specifications and standards, the frequency of test 
checks has been prescribed. 
5.2. NHAI also conducts ran dom Quality Inspection of the projects by involving retired 
senior government officials, as Independent Team Leaders.   Accordingly, quality checks are 
being carried out on various projects under implementation from time to time.

recordings of the specifications of the completed works, wherever possible, confirming that 
all works have been carried out by the concessionaire/contractors, before the grant of 
completion certificate of the road project to any concessionaire/contractor. This would 
ensure that ancillary specifications such as road signs, markings, shoulders etc. are duly

(Para 65) 
Reply of the Ministry 
9.1 As regard to compulsory submission of video recording to ensure specification of

ii. Before issue of provisional/final completion certificate

10. The Committee observes that land acquisition issues are at the core of delays faced in 
road projects. The Committee takes note of the guidelines issued by the Ministry to 
streamline acquisition of land for NH projects in the country and recommends that the 
Ministry may ensure that these guidelines may be re viewed from time to time, incorporating 
suitable modifications to simplify the process of land acquisition and ironing out the various 
constraints faced in land acquisition. 
(Para 71) 
Reply of the Ministry 
10.1 The observation of the Committee has been not ed and it has been decided to review 
the LA guidelines/manual. In the first instance, this Ministry has requested all concerned 
agencies to suggest necessary modification that needs to be incorporated in the proposed 
revised guidelines.   
Recommendation/Observation  
11. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may take immediate steps to ensure that 
adequate manpower is present with the land acquisition units at the field level across the 
country. The alignment given for any given project  should be finalized only after taking in 
inputs from all stakeholders and the local population, with due consideration to the future 
traffic projections, environmental concerns etc. Changing the alignment at a later stage of 
the project can be a costly af fair and should be avoided at all costs, through application of 
foresight. 
(Para 72) 
Reply of the Ministry 
11.1 The Ministry has authorised regional officer (s) to engage the services of retired 
revenue officials as Consultant (LA) for avoiding delay in Land Acquisition. Further, RO’s 
have been authorised to provide certain facilities such as furniture, office equipment’s, 
manpower etc., to CALAs for the purpose of acquiring land for NH Projects, from project 
contingencies. 
11.2 Also, of late, the Ministr y has requested all State Govt. for setting up of special Land 
Acquisition Unit (SLAU) for the work of Land Acquisition for National Highways across the 

8 
 
State. This will save considerable time in getting recommendations in individual cases and 
fast-track the process of Land Acquisition.  
Recommendation/Observation  
12.  The Committee desires to be apprised of the present status of the implementation of 
the Land Value Capture Mechanism. This mechanism may help the Ministry in managing the 
huge increase in road project costs on account of a significant jump in land acquisition costs 
in the past several years. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may consider making 
1the upfront contribution of State Governments flexible, fixing it on the basis of the f inancial 
ability of the State Government. 
(Para 74) 
Reply of the Ministry 
12.1 The revised policy on Value Capture Finance issued vide circular dated 18.03.2021 
envisages developing a mechanism to implement Value Capture Finance jointly by the States 
and NHAI, to part finance the cost of highway construction. This policy has no such 
condition for deposition of 50% cost of land acquisition by the State Government upfront. 
However, as per this policy circular, if the State Govt. provides at least 25% of the land 
acquisition cost for Ring Road/Bypasses, that project would be taken on priority. 
Recommendation/Observation  
13. The Committee feels that the Ministry may modify the land value capture mechanism 
in a way that the value captured by the State Government is, in part, be shared with the 
previous owners of the land. A major reason for the hesitation of land -owners to part with 
their land is that the land is often their only source of livelihood. A mechanism may be 
worked out where an upfront payment is made to the land -owner and they are guaranteed a 
payment in the form of annuity f or the long-term, financing the same through the land value 
captured by the State Government. The Committee believes that such a system would lower 
the frequency of land acquisition matters ending up in litigation, which cause huge delays to 
the projects, besides causing cost overruns. 
(Para 75) 
Reply of the Ministry 
13.1 Compensation is paid to the Land owners whose land is being acquired for 
development of National Highways. The determination of compensation is made in 
accordance with Section 26 &  First Schedule, rehabilitation and resettlement in accordance 
with the Second Schedule and infrastructure amenities in accordance with the Third Schedule 
of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and 
Resettlement ( RFCTLARR) Act, 2013. The land compensation includes Solatium @100% 
plus multiplication factor, additional market values and the compensation for trees and other 
assets. The compensation paid is substantially enhanced after implementation of RFCTLARR 
Act, 2013. 

9 
 
13.2 Generally, the acquisition of land for the National Highway, causes minimal 
displacement and dislocation of the affected persons. It would be more of an exception if the 
entire land-holding of a person/ family gets acquired in the process.  
13.3 The VCF policy basically envisages recovering the cost of highway development and 
also to part fund the other non -viable projects. It may not be possible to offer annuity out of 
this to landowners as it is not the profit earned but recovery of cost. 
Recommendation/Observation

contractors because of encumbrance on the land, once made available to them after 
acquisition. Further, the Ministry may urge upon the State Governments to carry out 
exercises to update their revenue maps periodically, in order to permit the Ministry to 
prepare more informed acquisition plans for its road projects. The Ministry may urge upon 
the State Governments to carry out exercises to updat e their revenue maps periodically, in 
order to permit the Ministry to prepare well-informed acquisition plans for its road projects.

informed acquisition plans for its road projects.

Reply of the Ministry 
15.1 The revised policy on Value Capture Finance issued vide circular dated 18.03.2021

16. The Committee takes note of the discrepancies pointed out by the Punjab PWD in the 
value of land determined at present based on registered sale deed/ collector rates and the 
actual market rate of the land. The Comm ittee feels that such discrepancy, if present, would 
invariably cause dissatisfaction among the land owners and the ensuing delays on account of 
arbitration and legal procedures cost the public exchequer a lot of money due to project cost 
overruns. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry may review the accuracy 
of the provisions existing at present in determining the amount of compensation to be paid to 
land-owners, as compared to the actual market value of the land. If substantial difference s 
are noticed in the compensation value and the market value in many instances, the Ministry 
may come up with a suitable mechanism for determination of a more fair value for the land to 
be acquired. 
(Para 94) 
Reply of the Ministry 
16.1 The compensation for the Land acquired for NH is determined in accordance with the 
First scheduled of the RFCTLARR ACT, 2013 with effect from 01.01.2015. As per Section 
26 of the RFCTLARR ACT, 2013, the market value of the land is determined as (a) the 
market value, if any specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deed 
or agreement to sale, as the case may be, in the area where the land is situated; or (b) the 
average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest vil lage or nearest vicinity 
area. The average sale price refer to in clause (b) is determined by taken into account the sale 
deeds of the agreement to sale registered for similar type of area in the near village or near 
vicinity during the year immediately pr eceding the issue of notification under Section 3A of 
the NH Act, 1956. The higher rate arrived from (a) and (b) above is adopted for 
determination for compensation of land acquisition in NH Projects  
16.2 Hence, the value of land which is more beneficial to the land owner is paid to him/her. 
It is a matter of fact that the Circle rate of land is notified by concerned State Governments 
and this Ministry has no role in this regard. 
Recommendation/Observation

Department, Assam and recommends that the Ministry may work to ensure that all the

Reply of the Ministry 
22.1 As regards overloading, Static Weigh Bridges  and Weigh in Motion Bridges have

issuance of challans is under th e jurisdiction of state police authorities with no role of NHAI.

22.2 However with respect to curbing of overloading at NH, following has been done

i. Rule 10 of NH Fee Rules , 2008  stipulates that a mechanical vehicle which is loaded 
in excess of permissible maximum gross vehicle weigh t in respect of such vehicles, 
shall not be permitted to use the National Highway or crossing the fee plaza until the 
excess load has been removed from such mechanical vehicle . 
ii. Rule 10 of NH Fee Rules 2008 prescribes rate of fee for overloading whereby 
overloaded vehicle are liable to pay applicable fees    of next higher category of 
vehicle. 
iii. The fee for overload has been amended   byMoRTH vide Gazette GSR 778(E) dated 
16.12.2013 of MoRTH whereby the ‘rate of fee for overloading’ was enhanced to 10

Highways Project. The Committee f eels that the Ministry must undertake a holistic review of 
the DPR preparation stage of road projects. Preparation of DPR should be aided by the 
latest technology available for the purpose and the inputs of the stakeholders and public 
representatives, incl uding the local M.P., and the demands and concerns of the local 
populace should be taken into account during the process of preparation of the DPR. The

stipulated period of time after the completion of the project, for any negligence on their part,

ensure ample provisions for road safety; mandatory service lanes; avoidance of traffic 
bottlenecks; and minimization of adverse environmental and heritage impact caused by the 
project. The Committee further recommends that traffic projections for the long-term must be

of the highways, when the widening of road is needed at a future date.

2.1 The Ministry adopts technologies like LiDAR, Satellite imaging, automated traffic 
counting system while preparing the detailed project report of a project. These technologies 
enable the Ministry to optimize road alignment and minimize the environmental impact of the 
project. The Ministry is committed to using state of the art technologies for the preparation of 
DPRs. 
2.2 The Ministry is considering a check and balance mechanism to hold th e concerned 
parties accountable for any negligence on their part across any stage in the execution of the 
project.  
2.3 Road safety and passenger comfort are of paramount importance to the Ministry. 
Wayside amenities and service lanes are planned on key ro ad stretches while ensuring road 
safety measures across all its projects. In addition, advanced traffic management system is 
being mandated across National Highways to ensure superior safety standards and real time 
incident response.

conceptualization of any new project and for flagship greenfield corridors, acquisition of

alignment is reviewed at the highest level to analyse the overall impact of the project – 
including the impact of land acquisition in displacement of population, the economic growth

Ministry, state level consultation is held with the respective state governments to ensure 
synergizing of highway network and other infrastructure network projects planned in the 
region. 
2.6 After the discussions are finalized with the state governments, an initial Land 
Acquisition Committee review of the alignment is conducted internally by the Ministry and 
approval is provided for initiating on -ground land acquisition process. Post t his, review of

project appraisal by Member of NHAI and senior officials of the Ministry. During the final 
approval of the project with the competent authority, inpu ts from external stakeholders like 
NITI Ayog are also sought to finalize the alignment and project features.  
2.7 In addition, the Project Directors and Regional Officers in NHAI have been 
empowered to suggest changes to alignment at the grass root level w ith inputs from local

26 
 
public, representation from different sections of the society are solicited in the presence of the

and inputs are incorporated in the finalization of the project alignment,  well before the 
initiation of land acquisition process with continuous inputs received through the project 
implementation units and regional offices across the country

Maintenance (O&M) of the road projects for the entire Concession Period (BOT (Toll) and 
BOT (Annuity) projects) or 15 years (HAM projects) in PPP projects, but in case of Public 
funded projects, the contractor is responsible for rectification of defects/ maintenance only 
during the defects/maintenance-cum-defects liability period which varies between one to four 
years. Since a large number of road projects are Public funded projects, especially the ones 
that are deemed not to be financially viable for private sector participation, the o nus of their 
maintenance falls on the Ministry/NHAI/State PWDs. In this regard, the Committee feels that 
the amount of funds allocated for the maintenance of National Highways every year is 
minuscule given the vast lengths of the National Highways across t he country. The 
Committee strongly recommends that the maintenance of the existing network of National 
Highways should be given topmost priority and the same should be reflected in the budgetary 
allocation made for the same. 
(Para 12)   
 Reply of Ministry 
1.1  Maintenance and Repair (M&R) of National Highways (NHs) is carried out for the 
stretches not covered under any programme or completed stretches where there are no 
liabilities of contractors to maintain such stretches. For the NH stretches developed on  EPC 
mode (Engineering, Procurement, Construction), the contractor is responsible for rectification 
of the defects and concurrent maintenance of project highway during the defect liability 
period after completion of the work. For the NH stretches developed  on BOT mode/ HAM, 
the Concessionaire is responsible for the maintenance of the project highway during the 
concession period. For some of the developed NH stretches through public funding, 
maintenance contracts have been taken up for a definite time period  (4 to 9 years) on 
Operation, Maintenance and Transfer (OMT) basis. Maintenance of the project highway 
under OMT contracts is the responsibility of the Concessionaire. 
1.2 For the remaining NH length, not covered under any programme, the Ministry 
allocates funds under for their M&R. Since inception of Bharatmala Pariyojana, Ministry is 
taking up more and more stretches under development and after development of these 
stretches, maintenance & operation is being done through contract, e.g. OMT, TOT etc. InvIT 
is also being initiated. Further, to overcome the shortfall in allocation under M&R head, the 
scheme of Periodical Repair/IRQP from Revenue Section (M&R) has been shifted to Capital 
Section (NH -O) w.e.f. 2021 -22. Hence, more fund is available for keeping the National 
Highways traffic worthy and no shortage of funds is anticipated at this stage.  
  

58 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation: 
1.3 The Committee feels that a large number of National Highways across the 
country are marred by dangerous potholes and need s to be maintained in a better state. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry may allocate some part of the 
maintenance budget to thoroughly monitor the vast network of National Highways 
across the country to be able to carry out the repair works of potholes within no times, 
which will enable to prevent any possible accidents due to poor state of NHs.

2.      The Committee reiterates the recommendation made in para 184 of its 287 th Report on 
Demands for Grants (2 021-22) of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, which is 
reproduced below verbatim. 
The Committee is of the view that roads across the country require frequent trenching 
for the purpose of laying of fiber lines, gas pipelines, and other similar amenities. The 
patchwork done thereafter is often delayed and rarely meets the desired construction 
quality, thus thwarting the speed of vehicles on the road and acting as a safety 
hazard. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may consider the inclusion of a 
provision for dedicated underground utility corridors in its upcoming National 
Highways projects to prevent frequent trenching. The provision for construction of 
dedicated underground utility corridor should be included at the DPR stage itself. The 
extra cost incurred for building the underground utility corridors may be replenished 
by monetizing the constructed utility corridors by charging the Departments and 
Companies which will benefit from avoid ance of frequent trenching of roads. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry may create a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) 
for the purpose of monetization of the utility corridors. 
 (Para 16) 
Reply of Ministry 
 
2.1    The Ministry agrees that the developme nt of essential utility corridors to lay down 
water pipelines, OFC cable, power line, drainage/sewerage network, gas pipelines etc. along 
with highway development shall be definitely time and cost saver as well as it will enhance 
economic viability and environment sustainability.  
2.2    This is to inform that the existing National Highway Right of Way (ROW) varies 
from 12 -60 m and depending upon the availability of space in ROW, permissions to lay 
utilities in a width of 2 m on extreme edges of ROW are bei ng given. As the different 
agencies approach this Ministry for such permissions at different timelines, the utility space is 
utilized mostly in an unorganized manner. While developing the National Highways of 
standards to serve projected future traffic, th e additional ROW is being acquired to make a 
consistent ROW of 30 -60 m. For a 4 -lane divided carriageway development, 45 -60 m ROW 

59 
 
is maintained through acquisition while for a 2 -lane paved shoulder development ROW upto 
30 m is maintained. Further the Natio nal Highways passes through rural and urban areas and 
in some cases, ROWs are compromised in urban areas.  
2.3    The need of utility corridors may also be divided into two parts i.e.   long distance 
utilities viz. OFC, gas/oil pipelines etc. passing through rural areas and short distance utilities 
viz. power lines, drainage/ sewerage, water pipelines etc. needing urban space. There are also 
security/safety & operational issues related to par allel and close running of power & OFC 
lines, power & gas/oil pipelines etc. 
Another area of concerns is: - 
i. The economical viability - whether such ducts are compulsorily to be built 
along highways without actual assessment of need in the area, or to be bu ilt 
on the basis of need after getting requirements from various agencies and 
ii. Cost of such ducts - cost sharing of construction of ducts and required land to 
be acquired specifically for such utility corridor, investments & tariff, 
operation & maintenance cost etc. 
2.4    In order to get all the above issues examined and to have a draft Policy Note/SOP, it has 
been decided by Ministry to take consultancy services of Andhra Pradesh Urban 
Infrastructure Asset Management Limited (APUIAML). Necessary instructio ns have been 
given to NHAI on 25th September 2020 to engage APUIAML. The draft policy so prepared 
shall be shared with all stake holders before its finalization. Based on the finalized policy, the 
decision on creation of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for  the purpose of monetization of 
the utility corridors may be taken. 
2.5  In this connection, APUIAML has recently submitted an interim feasibility report for 
laying of integrated utility corridors along greenfield NHs.   
 Further Recommendation/Observation: 
2.6  The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress made by the Ministry 
with regard to preparation of draft Policy Note/ SOP on the viability of having 
provisions for utility corridors and the decision regarding creation of a Special Purpose 
Vehicle for the purpose of monetization of the utility corridors, based on the finalized 
policy.

experience as well as professional qualifications.  
(Para 7.2) 
 
 The Committee feels that it might not be reasonable to assign heavy 
responsibilities to the existing officers with lesse r qualifications only to permit good 
promotional avenues to them. Only officers with enough experience and sufficient 
expertise should be granted the responsibility of high -level posts after carrying out the 
required assessment. Grant of timely financial upgradation may be considered for other 
officers. The Committee reiterates the recommendation made in para 7.2 of  Chapter III 
of this Report.  
(Para 9.3) 
 
 The Committee notes the various reasons behind the delays in completion of 
various road projects across the country. The Committee recommends that excepting 
the negative impact of the Coronavirus pandemic restrictions on the execution of 
projects, the Mini stry should take serious view of road projects being delayed on 
account of below -par performance by road contractors/ concessionaires. A mechanism 
may be put in place to award the road contract to a different concessionaire once a 
delay in execution has oc curred because of the existing concessionaire. The previous 

99 
 
performance of concessionaires may be taken into  consideration for award of future 
road project contracts.  
(Para 10.3) 
 
 The Committee desires to be apprised of the progress made by the Ministry in 
this regard.  
(Para 11.2) 
 
 The Committee desires to be apprised of the action taken by the Ministry to 
request formation of a panel of retired judges having expertise in infrastructural 
litigations in order to enable quicker judgements in case of disputes with 
concessionaires.  
(Para 12.2) 
 
 The Committee recommends that NHAI may give due importance to improving 
the Sukhad Yatra mobile application since the data submitted by the app users can help 
NHAI a lot in monitoring the state of National High ways across the country. User 
feedback received on the various application distribution platforms such as Google Play 
Store and Apple App Store, may be duly factored in future updates of the application 
and the data received from the users.  
(Para 13.3) 
 
 The Committee feels that the number of complaints received by NHAI through 
the app are minuscule, given the vast network of NHs across the country. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry and NHAI may promote the Sukhad Yatra 
app through social media an d other means, so as to gain crucial information about 
requirement of maintenance of National Highways, which will also help in preventing 
the occurrence of road accidents due to poor state of Highways.  
(Para 14.3) 
  
 The Committee feels that without the existence of a central database, it would 
not be possible for the Ministry/NHAI to keep track of the road projects across the 
country that have been awarded to a concessionaire. The Committee, therefore, may be 
updated about the action taken by NHAI to cre ate and maintain a central database of 
road projects awarded to various concessionaires so as to permit NHAI to factor in the 
contract award history and performance history of a given concessionaire before 
awarding them a new road project.  
(Para 15.3) 
 
 The Committee recommends that the knowledge gained from such regular 
meetings with the lenders may be utilized to periodically update and revise the Model 

100 
 
Concession Agreement so as to encourage lenders to finance a higher number of 
National Highway projects.  
(Para 16.2) 
 
 The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 16.2 of  Chapter III 
of this Report.  
(Para 17.2) 
 
 The Committee had been informed by various financial institutions  that the 
construction of parallel roads is a major issue faced by them causing loss of revenue on 
tolled projects. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its original recommend ation that 
the Ministry may introduce appropriate rules/laws to ensure that const ruction of 
parallel roads by State or other agencies may be avoided at all costs and some sort of 
provision for payment of compensation to the concessionaire may be considered  by the 
Ministry.  
(Para 19.2) 
 
 The Committee recommends that the task of creating new PIUs may be 
completed at the earliest so as to share the workload of the overburdened PIUs. The 
Committee further recommends that action may be taken at the earliest indications of a 
project running of f-schedule and the performance of the concessionaires in terms of 
progress of work completed may be monitored closely for all road projects across the 
country.  
(Para 20.5 
 
 The Committee notes that the reply of the Ministry does not furnish any 
information regarding why the SARDP -NE Phase -B cannot be taken up along with 
SARDP-NE Phase A, since implementing both Phases in parallel might help complete 
the SARDP-NE programme at a quicker pace. The Committee, therefore, desires to be 
apprised of the reasons for not considering parallel execution of both Phases of SARDP-
NE.  
(Para 21.2) 
 
 The Committee notes the efforts made by the Ministry for timely execution of 
projects under SARDP -NE but given the huge delays that are currently faced in the 
programme, the Committee recommends that the Ministry may undertake a holistic 
review of the reasons for which the remedial efforts of the Ministry are not effective in 
resolving the delays being faced in SARDP-NE.  
(Para 22.2) 
  
 

101 
 
 The C ommittee feels that awarding road projects, especially in the North -East 
region, to the lowest bidder might be leading to below -par quality of roads being 
constructed, besides incapable concessionaires causing delays in road projects because 
of their financial and technical incapacities. T he Committee, therefore, reiterates its 
recommendation made in Para 26 of its 296 th Report, which is reproduced below 
verbatim: 
“The Committee further recommends the Ministry to carefully analyze the 
shortcomings of the existing mechanism for awarding road  projects to the lowest 
bidder, since doing so includes little thought for ensuring quality of the work. The 
Committee believes that there should be consideration for other importance factors 
besides the bidding amount, while awarding a project to a conces sionaire. A 
qualitative approach must be formulated for awarding road projects. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry may take up with the Central Vigilance 
Commission (CVC), the shortcomings of the existing system of awarding a project 
to the lowest bidder, presenting its arguments for modification of the CVC 
guidelines for awarding of tender in a suitable way to permit an element of 
qualitative approach in the tender awarding process for road projects. The 
Committee feels that a criterion may be deve loped where certain weightage is given 
to objective parameters such as the awards presently being executed by the 
contractor, their financial record, and most importantly, the past performance of a 
contractor, in terms of quality of work and timely executi on. The database 
recommended by the Committee in para 22 of this Report may be useful for such 
purposes.” 
(Para 23.2) 
 
 The Committee recommends that the Ministry may lay special focus on timely 
completion of road projects in LWE affected areas in close co ordination with local law 
enforcement and other concerned departments.  
(Para 24.2) 
 
 The Committee may be apprised of the details of the various research activities 
that are being carried out by the SRD& Q Division of NHAI. The Committee further 
recommends that the Ministry may consider increasing the budget for research 
purposes in the upcoming years so as to allow research for improving construction 
quality in hilly and flood -prone regions, improving roa d safety across the country and 
developing a mechanism to effectively monitor the pliability of National Highways 
across the country so as to proactively prevent accidents from happening because of 
shoddy quality of roads.  
(Para 25.2) 
 
 The Committee notes the various steps being taken by the Ministry and the 
policy guidelines brought out by NHAI to improve road safety across the country but 
feels that given the ever-increasing number of deaths occurring due to road accidents in 
the country, a lot more  needs to be done urgently in order to minimize the same. The 

102 
 
Committee recommends that the Ministry/NHAI may review the safety audit process 
itself and ensure that the same is carried out in a transparent and honest manner. The 
Committee further recommend s that the identified black spots may be rectified at the 
earliest and the definition for identification of black spots may be tightened so as to 
identify and rectify more accident-prone spots across the NH network in the country.  
(Para 26.3) 
 
 The Committee recommends that the Ministry may speed up the process of 
rectification of black spots that have already been identified since these spots are very 
likely to cause more accidents if left unrectified. The status of all black spots may be 
kept regularly updated on the NHAI website and any delay in the rectification of black 
spots may be looked into urgently.  
(Para 27.3) 
 
 The Committee recommends that the tender for Computer Aided Dispatch 
System may be finalized at the earliest since providing timely emergency care during 
the golden hour can help save countless lives involved in road accidents across the 
country. The Committee desires to be kept apprised in this regard.   
(Para 28.2) 
 
 The Committee recommends that dedicated efforts may be made to promote the 
tollfree helpline number 1033 amongst highway users. The Committee may be apprised 
of the action taken by the Ministry to promote the usage of the number 1033 through 
social media and other means.  
(Para 29.2) 
 
 The Committee appreciates the  efforts of the Ministry to rope in the private 
sector by vesting Driving Training Centres with functions such as testing of aspirants 
for issuance of driving licence, which will hopefully make such centres a successful 
business proposition. Having well -trained drivers on the Indian roads would go a long 
way in improving road safety and aiming to have Driving Training Centres in all 
districts of the country would be the first step towards that. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry may cons ider providing some aid to the interested 
parties in terms of lending for setting up such Driving Training Centres, in 
collaboration with financial institutions.  
(Para 30.6) 
 
 The Committee recommends that latest safety standards adopted for vehicles 
globally, may be suitably incorporated in the Indian vehicle safety standards from time 
to time, so as to minimize the number of deaths occurring on Indian roads due to road 
accidents.  

103 
 
(Para 31.4) 
 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry would be able to complete the remaining 
projects under the Char dham Pariyojana within the targeted date of completion of 
December, 2024. The Committee recommends that all possible measures may be taken 
from the planning stage itself to ensure that the road projects of the M inistry cause 
minimal impact on the environment, especially in eco -sensitive hilly regions. This would 
help lower the delays faced on account of Court litigations and petitions in the NGT.  
(Para 32.2) 
 
 The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 32.2 of  Chapter III 
of this Report.  
(Para 33.3) 
 
 The Committee notes the reply. The Committee further recommends that in 
future, such Rapid Environmental Impact Assessment may be proactively carried out 
by the Ministry for all of its major National Highways projects in ecologically sensitive 
regions.  
(Para 34.2) 
 
 The Committee may be apprised about the action taken by the Ministry in this 
regard.  
(Para 35.2) 
 
 The Committee notes the advisories put in place at present by the Ministry with 
regard to PUC centres. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may  consider 
incorporation of stricter guidelines in its advisory  in order to curb malpractices that 
allow polluting vehicles to pass the pollution test, by way of video recording when 
pollution tests are conducted.  
(Para 36.8) 
 
 The Committee recommends that NHAI may include the option to report 
requirement of maintenance of roadside plantations on National Highways, so that 
highway users can bring such requirement to the notice of NHAI for timely  action. 
Besides, NHAI may ensure that such maintenance activities are carried out periodically 
without fail, since overgrown trees and bushes can lead to visibility issues, which in turn 
can lead to lethal accidents.  
(Para 37.5) 
 

104 
 
 The Committee recommend s that guidelines similar to those that have been 
issued regarding construction of bridge structures passing over declared National 
Waterways, may be issued for construction of such bridge structures over other inland 
waterways as well. The guidelines in t his regard may be framed in close coordination 
with the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and other concerned departments. 
The Committee feels that doing it is necessary to ensure the development of road 
infrastructure may not cause hindrance in us age of inland waterways as a means of 
transportation.  
(Para 38.2)

Aviation on the recommendations/observations as contained in its Two Hundred Ninety 
Seventh Report on the subject ‘Functioning of Airports Authority of India’ which was 
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 2nd August, 2021.  
 
2.  The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 16th December, 2021 
in respect of all the observations/ recommendations contained in the Report. The repl ies have 
been categorized as follows:-

Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry: 
Paragraph Nos.:  9.8, 10.8, 10.9, 10.10, 10.12, 11.10, 11.11, 12.3, 12.7, 13.9, 18.5, 
18.6, 22.3, 30.12, 31.1 and 33.

2 
 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
Air Traffic Services 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Committee recommends that a High Powered Committee should be constituted 
both for flexi air space management and issues related to Civil Enclaves to address these 
issues comprehensively. 
(Para 9.8) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 NHLAPB (National High Level Airspace Policy Body) has been constituted in 2013 
for the flexible use of Airspace  (FUA) in accordance with the FUA Manual approved by 
Government of India in 2011  
1.2 Based on the directives of Government of India under the AtmaNirbhar Bharat 
Abhiyan (ANB), AAI had taken up issue of e fficient use of airspace usi ng Flexible Use of 
Airspace concept with IAF, Indian Navy and HAL for optimum use of airspace in May 2020. 
The airspace released on daily basis is being utilized by all stakeholders. 
1.3 Actions Taken:- 
(i) 116 Conditional Routes (CDRs) implemented. 
 
(ii) National Airspace Management Cells (NAMC) at Delhi Air Traffic Flow 
Management (ATFM) centre and Regional Airspace Management Cells (RAMC) 
at Delhi (IGIA) & Chennai Airport have been established. 
(iii) Upper Airspace of 46 Restricted Areas of IAF has been converted as Temporary 
Reserved Airspace (TRA). 
(iv) 24 Danger Areas of Army de-notified. Upper limit of Two Danger Areas lowered 
to 10000 ft Above Mean Sea Level (AMSL). 
(v) Five new CDR proposals sent to IAF for concurrence in September 2021. 
 
Development, Upgradation and Modernization of Airports 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee underlines the need for a well chalked out Master Plan with regard to 
aviation infrastructure, in order to ensure that the requirements of the growth in the civil 

3 
 
aviation sector are properly catered to. The Committee urges the Ministry to ensure that 
adequate parking space and landing slots are available at the airports. 
(Para 10.8) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 All Airports are being comprehensively planned and develo ped considering 30 years 
forecast. Accordingly, land is earmarked/ additional land is requested from State 
Governments based on long-term futuristic development of single runway or parallel runway 
configurations and the type of aircraft expected to operate  in future considering the potential 
of traffic it will be handling. Due to the dynamic nature of development, the Master Plans are 
reviewed regularly based on the revised growth forecast. 
2.2 Based on the futuristic traffic projections adequate Aircraft parking bays and slot 
management are created and planned at the airports, such that it would be able to meet all the 
future traffic demand. 
2.3 Around Rs.  90,000 crores of investments are expected to be pumped into Civil 
Aviation Sector in the next 5 years  out of which AAI alone will invest Rs.25000 crores for 
infrastructure creation. The remaining approx. Rs. 65,000 is being spent by the private sector. 
2.4 To meet the demand, AAI has embarked upon a capital expenditure (CAPEX) plan of 
Rs. 25000 crores in next five years for development / modernization / up gradation of airport 
infrastructure projects of AAI airports in the country.   418 additional parking bays are 
planned at various AAI airports in next five years for night parking of new aircrafts being

Air Traffic Services 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Committee is of the considered opinion that keeping in view the exponential air 
traffic growth witnessed in the country in the past few years, it is essential that best 
international practices as regards the Air Navigatio n Services are adopted and implemented 
in the country. The Committee strongly feels that a futuristic Master Plan for Air Navigation 
Services is inevitable so that substantial benefits are accrued to all the stakeholders. The 
Committee emphasizes the need to ensure strict adherence to the international standards of 
safety and security. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure that steps 
should be taken to upgrade the ANS facilities and procedures and to give due emphasis on 
research, development and training.  
(Para 9.3) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 Airports Authority of India (AAI) is continuously upgrading its Air Navigation 
Services (ANS) Infrastructure to meet the air traffic growth. AAI has undertaken Upper 
Airspace Harmonization (UAH) Programme for better capacity and efficiency facilitating 
safe and seamless movement of air traffic within Indian airspace. Harmonization of Chennai 
and Kolkata airspace has been completed. 
1.2 The entire terrestrial airspace of India is under surveillance  coverage through a 
network of Primary & Secondary Radar and Automatic Dependent Surveiilance -Broadcast 
(ADS-B) surveillance system. From January 2020, the entire oceanic airspace controlled by 
AAI has been brought under surveillance coverage by hiring Satellite based ADS-B services. 
1.3 The communication facilities have been upgraded to Internet Protocol (IP) based 
technology for seamless coverage. AAI has established Futuristic Telecomm Infrastructure 
(FTI). It is a Service Level Agreement (SLA) based sys tem ensuring 99.99% to 99.999% 
availability, using latest technology and communication infrastructure at each AAI location. 
This will help improve airspace safety, capacity, and efficiency. ATM Automation equipment 
completing its lifecycle are continuously  upgraded. AAI planned to upgrade/ replace ATC 
automation System at 38 airports to modernize the ATC System. 
1.4 For optimum use of airport resources and airspace and thus reducing airspace/airport 
congestion AAI has implemented Central Air Traffic Flow Ma nagement (C -ATFM) from 
2017. This will also reduce environmental impact due to less emission and helping fuel 
saving by airlines. 

13 
 
1.5 To continue this modernization effort to meet the future demand, Airports Authority 
of India (AAI) entered into an agreeme nt with United States Trade and Development Agency 
(USTDA) to develop a Communications, Navigation and Surveillance/Air Traffic 
Management (CNS/ATM) roadmap to improve airspace utilization and implement 
CNS/ATM air and ground infrastructure in the short, m edium and long term (upto 10 years)  
for modernization on 16th November, 2018. 
1.6 The study has been carried out by M/s Boeing, USA in consultation with all 
stakeholders such as Airlines, Airport Operators, DGCA and AAI to assist AAI in preparing a 
futuristic comprehensive Masterplan for CNS and ATM facilities and services along with 
guidance on implementation process and regulatory requirements.    
1.7 The report has been submitted by M/s Boeing in October 2021.Based on this 
document, AAI will prepare its roadmap by December 2022 for next 10 years .The Roadmap 
will be dovetailed with th e National Air Navigation Plan to be developed by MoCA , which 
is an ICAO requirement. 
1.8 AAI is upgrading its ANS training facilities with state -of-the-art Training simulators 
(such as Aerodrome Tower Visual Simulator, Flight Simulator Training Device, A TC 
Procedural Simulator, ATC Radar Simulator) as part of training improvement plan.    
1.9 To promote Research & Development in Civil Aviation, AAI is developing a Civil 
Aviation Research Organization (CARO) at Hyderabad. The establishment will provide an 
integrated platform for all Indian stakeholders. 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee hopes that Modernization of Military Airfields (MAFI) project which 
is a turn key project, would enhance the operational capability, by facilitating air operations 
of civilian aircrafts, even in poor visibility and adverse weather conditions, while enhancing 
aerospace safety. The Committee observes that MAFI project of the Indian Air Force should 
decide and cull out those activities which are primarily nav igational equipment including 
approach landing systems, PAPI runway lights, threshold lights, instruments and equipment 
etc., where AAI/ATS have a unique advantage, as they have been handling these systems 
across the country, for over seven decades. Domest ic civil aviation safety is the primary 
responsibility of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, DGCA and AAI. The utilization of these 
navigational aids/approach landing systems/equipment etc., which have been installed across 
the country, is primarily done by t he AAI, which has domain knowledge. They are also 
familiar with the quality procurement processes, maintenance and operational requirements 
of these instruments which they have been using for Civil operations for over fifty years. The 
Committee recommends that a High Level Committee may be created with the Indian Air 
Force to cull out those activities related to navigation and landing facilities which are, 
primarily, in the domain knowledge, with the AAI for Civil operations. The Committee 
recommends that a part from this, the development of the rest of the infrastructure planned 
under the MAFI scheme may continue as envisaged, for a greater synergy between civil 
aviation requirements and operational requirements of Indian Air Force. 

14 
 
(Para 9.7) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 Since the military airfields are owned and operated by the Defence Forces, based on 
their operational requirements and infrastructure on ground, it is felt that it is not feasible to 
cull out those activities related to navigational equipment i ncluding approach landing 
systems, PAPI runway lights, threshold lights, instruments and equipment etc. as 
recommended because the military requirement may not be compatible with the civil aviation 
requirement. 
2.2 However as recommended by the committee, it is noted for compliance and the 
recommendations have been sent to Ministry of Defence (MoD) for their comments.

Recommendation/Observation  
9. The Committee understands that a major deterrent for the growth of the MRO 
industry is high taxation of MRO components. The Committee strongly recommends that the 
Ministry should give necessary focus on the issues presently faced in the MRO sector in order 
to ensure that India evolves into a key international player in offering MRO facilities. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should take necessary steps to ensure that MRO 
workshops are set up in all the me tro cities in the country, in order to attract international 
business. The Committee also emphasizes the need for enhanced collaboration between 
defence and civil MROs.

19 
 
9.1 Investment decisions in any industry including MROs are dependent on various 
factors which include market forces and regulatory environment. Government has taken 
several measures for a more congenial regulatory environment. In September 2021, Ministry 
of C ivil Aviation (MoCA) announced a new MRO policy, which includes leasing of land 
through open tenders and abolishing royalty charged by the Airport Authority of India (AAI) 
for the Maintenance Repair and Overhaul (MRO) business for ease of doing business an d to 
provide further incentive to the sector. Other key measures undertaken for supporting the 
growth of the Indian MRO sector include the following:  
(i) GST on MRO has been reduced from 18% to 5% with full Input Tax Credit from 
1 April 2020. 
(ii) Custom duty has been waived on tools, toolkits and spares imported by MROs. 
(iii) Transactions sub-contracted by foreign OEMs/MRO to domestic MRO are treated 
as “exports” with zero-rated GST from 1 April 2020. 
(iv) Relaxed restriction on utilization of duty-free parts from one year to three years. 
(v) The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has come up with a business -friendly 
proposal for MRO with zero airport royalty charges and significantly rationalised 
land rentals for eight AAI airports (Begumpet, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Chennai, 
Delhi, Juhu, Kolkata and Tirupati). 
(vi) Stay of foreign aircraft for MRO in India permitted till completion of MRO work 
or six months, whichever is earlier. 
(vii) Rules simplified for export of leased aircraft in complete or knocked -down 
conditions, opening up new opportun ities in redelivery checks and aircraft 
component recycling. 
(viii) Aircraft lessors are being encouraged to carry out their end -of-lease checks in 
India. 
(ix) Foreign manufacturers are being encouraged to set up their MRO facilities on 
their own or through joint ventures with Indian players.  
9.2 The Government is facilitating civil -military MRO convergence by fostering greater 
technical and business collaboration between leading MRO companies in India and the 
defence establishment.

large towns; and many parts of the country still remain unconnected by air services. 
Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should take urgent 
effective steps to ensure adequate air connectivity in different parts of the country under RCS.
