RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS AT A GLANCE 
 
CHAPTER-III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF 
THE MINISTRY HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
The Committee does not find the reply given by the Ministry to be satisfactory. 
The Committee notes that given the considerable gap between its projected demand 
and actual allocation  made at BE 2022 -23, the Ministry will project a well enhanced 
demand at RE 2022 -23. However, the Ministry has not furnished any information 
regarding the reasons for projecting a significantly lower demand of Rs. 3357.45 crores 
in BE 2022-23 as compared to the projection of Rs. 3843.68 crore in BE 2021 -22 by the 
Ministry. The Committee may be apprised of the specific reasons which led to a 
substantial decrease in the projected demand of the Ministry at BE 2022 -23 as 
compared to its demand at BE 2021-22. 
(Para 1.2) 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
 
The Committee notes that the reply furnished by the Ministry does not make 
any mention of the steps taken by the Ministry/ASI to ensure optimal utilization of 
funds available with ASI and proper allocation of funds across competing ends. The 
Committee desires to be apprised in this regard, in light of the substantial increase in 
the budgetary allocation available with ASI for the FY 2022-23. 
 
(Para 2.4) 
 
The Ministry does not mention target of employment generation in its reply. The 
Ministry should set the goal for employment generation in the aftermath of the 
Coronavirus pandemic. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Culture and 
ASI should work in close coordination with the Ministry of Tourism and ensure th at 
besides carrying out its mandate, one of the primary goals of the activities/schemes 
planned by the Ministry of Culture/ASI should be to bolster the tourism prospects of a 
region wherein such monuments exist. 
(Para 3.2) 
DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUMS 
 
The Committee had originally recommended that the Ministry should formulate 
a document indicating the present as well as future human resource needs of the Indian 
Museums sector for consideration of the Indian Institute of Heritage, in its 294 th Report 
which was presented to the Parliament on 26 th July, 2021. The Committee desires to be 
apprised of the specific action taken by the Ministry till now for the formulation of this 
document, which would be of critical importance to ensure that the upcoming Indian 
Institute of Heritage is well -equipped to adequately meet the human resource needs of 
the Indian Museums sector in the future. 
(Para 4.2) 

32 
 
VACANCIES IN VARIOUS ORGANIZATIONS OF THE MINISTRY 
 
The Committee is not satisfied by the explanation furnished by the Mi nistry with 
regard to the vacancies existing in ASI. The Committee appreciates that filling up of 
posts through direct recruitment is a time consuming process. However, this delay can 
be anticipated well in advance by ASI, given most vacancies arise out of  retirement of 
employees. The Committee, therefore, recommends that ASI must execute its 
recruitment process sufficiently in advance keeping in mind the retirement schedule of 
its existing employees, as well as the average time it takes to fill vacancies through direct 
recruitment, so as to ensure that it is adequately staffed at all points of time, which, in 
turn, will ensure that ASI can carry out its mandate in an effective manner.   
(Para 5.3) 
The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 5.3  of this Report, 
for all organizations under the Ministry of Culture so as to ensure adequate staffing at 
all times.                                                                                                          (Para 6.2) 
 
The Committee would like to know the present status of the above vacancies and 
revival of posts. 
(Para 7.2) 
NORTH-EASTERN AREAS 
 
The Committee is surprised to note that whereas the overall expenditure 
incurred by the Ministry in the past 5 years depicts a satisfactory pattern  of utilization 
of the funds allocated to the Ministry, the expenditure made by the Ministry against the 
total allocation for the North -East Region shows a consistent pattern of 
underutilization. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may take a serious look 
into the possible reasons behind this pattern of underutilization and take urgent action 
to rectify the same in the coming years so as to ensure that the funds available for 
preservation and conservation of the rich tangible and intangible cultural heritage of 
the North-Eastern Region, are optimally utilized. 
(Para 8.2) 
 
NATIONAL MISSION ON CULTURAL MAPPING AND ROADMAP 
 
The Committee is concerned to note a consistent pattern of underutilization of 
funds under the head „National Mission of Cultural Ma pping and Roadmap‟, under 
which data mapping, demography building, formalizing the processes and bringing all 
cultural activities under one umbrella for better results, etc. is done. The Committee is 
of the view that the clear pattern of underutilization u nder this head, especially during 
the year 2021 -22, hints at the lackadaisical approach of the Ministry towards the 
important activities envisaged to be carried out under this head. Effective measures 
may be taken to ensure that the activities planned for each year under this head are 
carried out as per schedule and optimal utilization of funds is achieved. 
(Para 9.2)

CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee observes that infrastructure for tourism includes basic infrastructure 
components like roads, railways, airports, water, electricity, hotels etc. The Committee 
recommends that interconnectivity of roads, ports, airports, railways and waterways should be 
part of the infrastructure planning process while preparing the Detailed Appraisal Report of any 
Tourism project. Service roads and linkage of nearby places should also be included. Transport 
infrastructure plays a vital role in connecting origin and destination locations while ensuring 
safe, comfortable and efficient transportation to tourists. While evaluating travel experiences, 
transport is o ne of the main factors which has a great bearing on trip satisfaction. The 
Committee therefore recommends that multi -modal transport should be envisaged while 
preparing DPR for facilitating tourism in the country. This will not only facilitate free flowing  
traffic but also serve to make tourist destinations more attractive and accessible. 
(Para 13) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 The suggestion of the Committee is noted. However, it may be mentioned that the 
Ministry of Tourism under its „Swadesh Darshan Scheme‟ has sanctioned funds for development 
of last mile connectivity. The Ministry of Tourism has now revamped its „Swadesh Darshan 
Scheme‟ in the form of Swadesh Darshan 2.0. The guidelines of SD 2.0 have an illustrative list 
of components which can enhance to urism potential of the destination and the same includes 
components pertaining to connectivity, wayside amenities & parking. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee is of the opinion that in order to successfully implement tourism 
infrastructural Schemes, the state governments should carry out due diligence in consultation 
with the nodal agencies during conceptualizing the projects and ensure the completion of 
tendering process of projects in a time bound manner to enable the Ministry to release fu nds for 
such projects. The Committee recommends the Ministry to create a mechanism for proactive 
project monitoring and reviewing the same to avoid delays in implementation as per agreed 
schedules and in compliance with the approved DPRs. 
(Para 16) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 The recommendation of the Committee is noted. The Ministry of Tourism has 
incorporated due provisions pertaining to monitoring & reviewing of sanctioned projects in the 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 guidelines.

PRASHAD Scheme and building them as tourist hubs available on cheaper tickets will attract 
tourists searching for a tranquil beach-like affordable and less crowded environment, which will

(Para 24)

(Para 32) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1 The recommendation of the Committee is noted.

GENERATING REVENUE AND OVERALL TOURIST SATISFACTION  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. Proper revenue -generation in a developing country leads to innovation - in the 
production, services and pricing sectors, opens new gates of employment, resource sharing, 

4 
 
education, empowerment of general people, improvement of political relations and reforming the

(Para 51) 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1 The recommendation of the Committee is noted. 
 
 
PROMOTION AND PUBLICITY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. The Committee observes that modern tourism industry is a key driver of socioeconomic 
growth through creation of jobs, infrastructure development, and the export revenues earned 
because it has  potential to stimulate other sectors through its backward and forward linkages 
and cross -sectoral synergies with airlines, transport, basic infrastructure like hotels, guides, 
road connectivity, agriculture, handicrafts etc. The Committee notes that despi te the fact that 
India offers a diverse portfolio for travel, tourism and hospitality, the share of its International 
Tourist Arrivals (ITAs) is merely 1.59% in 2021. With the obvious that there is an increased 
competition among various countries to attract more foreign visitors, it is an imperative need for 
India to prepare a better marketing strategy by hiring marketing experts to attract foreign 
visitors. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should formulate an integrated 
marketing and promotional strategy in collaboration with a professional body to carry out 
market research to identify expectations, requirements, psychographics, demographics and many 
other aspects of a foreign tourist willing to travel to India, thereby enabling to cre ate a strategic 
plan to revive the pandemic-hit tourism sector. The Committee feels that one of the effective steps 
in this direction would be re-casting the website of the Ministry in an attractive and user-friendly 
manner. 
(Para 56) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
7.1 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. It may however be mentioned 
that the Ministry of Tourism promotes tourism to India in potential international markets and 
within India through various measures. Ministry of Tourism releases domestic and international 
print, electronic and online media campaigns under the „Incredible India‟ brand -line, 
participates/organizes seminars/conventions, Road Shows/travel fairs/exhibitions, tourism related 
conferences/and other promotional activities to promote various tourism destinatio ns and 
products of the country. The promotions are also undertaken through the Website 
(www.incredibleindia.org) and the Social Media platforms of the Ministry. 
 
7.2 In addition, the Ministry of Tourism through its India Tourism Offices Overseas along 
with Indian Missions abroad endeavors to position India as a preferred tourism destination in the 
tourism generating markets to promote various tourism products and destinations including 
Indian culture and to increase India‟s share in the global tourism market. On the re quest of 
Ministry of Tourism, the Ministry of External Affairs has designated Tourism Officers in the 
Indian Missions of top 20 source markets in October, 2021. Country specific strategy papers 

5 
 
have been prepared by designated Tourism officers posted in In dian Missions overseas for 
promotion of Incredible India in the respective countries. 
 
7.3 Ministry of Tourism is also in the process of revamping the Incredible India Digital 
Platform. Various elements like personalization, multiple interface, multiple languages, emphasis 
on AR/8D contents, interactive map, trip planner, experiences, and Omni -channel campaigns are 
being planned for revamping Incredible India Digital Platform.

CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee observes that in its earlier report, it had noted that only one of the fifteen 
thematic circuits under the ‘Swadesh Darshan Schem e’ had been completed till that time and 
had recorded its disappointment about the slow progress in the projects under the Scheme. Now, 
since all the projects under the Scheme are being reviewed, the Committee urges the Ministry to 
complete the review in a time bound manner so that the Scheme may be completed without undue 
delay. Since the projects under the Scheme are spread throughout the country and involve local 
bodies, the Committee recommends the Ministry to hear the views of all stakeholders involved  or 
ensure that the agencies implementing the Scheme do so, and take due cognizance of local 
sentiment so that once streamlined the projects under the Scheme would be able to be 
implemented without any hindrance. The Committee also recommends that the yard stick to 
review the project should only be whether it would be truly effective in increasing the tourist 
potential of the area. 
(Para 14) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 „Swadesh Darshan Scheme‟ has been revamped as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD 2.0) under 
which it is envisaged that responsible and sustainable tourism destinations will be developed 
after following a destination and tourist centric approach. The Ministry of Touri sm has now 
issued the guidelines for Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme.  
 
1.2 As per the guidelines for SD2.0 scheme, the State will set up a Destination Management 
Committee (DMC) at the district level under the Chairmanship of District Collector. The 
Chairperson may invite the representatives of any other Department or organization, as may be 
required as special invitee. 
 
1.3 The function of the DMC includes bringing synergy in the efforts of various departments 
and organizations towards promotion of the tourism and will have the following functions: 
(i) To review the implementation of the scheme on ground and resolve the bottlenecks in 
the implementation. 
(ii) To provide synergy with other schemes and programs of Central and State Government 
at the district level particu larly relating to infrastructure development, human capital 
development, job creation and entrepreneurship, investment promotion and marketing 
and other such programs to develop and promote tourism. 
(iii) To review Operation and Management arrangement particular ly health, hygiene, safety 
and overall quality of maintenance of the destination. 
(iv) To promote skill development and local entrepreneurship for various tourism services.  
(v) To perform all other functions of a Destination Management Organization to promote 
the destination for domestic and international tourists.

(Para 15) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 The Ministry of Tourism has now revamped its „Swadesh Darshan Scheme‟  as SD 2.0 
and as per the guidelines for SD  2.0 Scheme. Restoration, conserva tion, illumination of 
monuments/heritage structures is included as Tourism Core Products in the illustrative list of

2.2 It may also be mentioned that Ministry of Tourism promotes India in a holistic manner

mediums. Promotions are also undertaken through the website www.incredibleindia.org and 
social media platforms of the Ministry. 
 
 
PRASHAD SCHEME 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3 The Committee observes that religious tourism is unlike leisure tourism in as much that 
in building a religious tourism product, it is essential to build in community participation at the 
given location. The participation of loca l nodal agencies along with State Governments in the 
PRASHAD Scheme is therefore of utmost importance and the Ministry should endeavour to make 
all efforts to ensure their involvement and not leave it to the responsibility of the State 
Governments alone. 
(Para 21) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1 Under PRASHAD scheme, the local bodies, Panchayats and the officials of State 
Governments are an essential part of the decision making for finalizing the projects and their 
involvement is inevitable. All the project proposals received in the Division are recommended by 
the State Governments in consultation with the local stakeholders which include the religious 
trusts, locally elected representatives etc. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
4 The Committee is of the view religi ous tourists come from all economic strata and there 
is enormous need for hotels especially in the Budget and Economy categories. The Committee is 
also of the opinion that local families willing to provide homemade food and homestay facilities 
in their abodes to the tourists should be identified and given training by the Ministry in handling 
the process to promote local Indian cuisine among foreign tourists and at international level. 

8 
 
The Committee is sanguine that such a novel step will unlock job opportun ities for Indian 
families and generate resources for huge revenue potential in the Indian tourism sector. 
(Para 22)  
 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1 In order to augment supply of hotel accommodation for budget tourists, the Ministry has 
voluntary schemes for approval of Guest Houses, Incredible India Bed and Breakfast 
Establishments and Incredible India Homestay Establishments. The Voluntary scheme of the 
Ministry of Tourism for approval of hotels at project stage and classification stage stipulate that 
the hotels of 1, 2, 3 and 4 star categories availing subsidy/tax benefits/other benefits from the 
Central/State Government would be subject to a lock -in period of 8 years during which they 
would not seek upgradation to a higher category so that these hotels cont inue to serve as budget 
category hotels. The Ministry of Tourism has also requested the State Governments/UT 
Administrations to give due weightage to development of mid segment hotels which typically 
will fall in 3 star and 4 star categories while earmarking/auctioning of land for developing hotels. 
4.2 Further, the Ministry of Tourism has prepared a National Strategy for promotion of Rural 
Homestays in line with the national strategies for Rural Tourism and Sustainable Tourism which 
has been circulated to Central Ministries, State Governments & Industry Associations. The 
Strategy aims at recognizing the role of rural homestays in promoting Rural and Sustainable 
Tourism and strengthening the support system for rural homestays. 
 
4.3 The Ministry of Tourism has a Home -stay (Multi-Skilled Caretaker) training programme 
under the “Capacity Building for Service Providers” (CBSP) scheme. It is informed that training 
as part of the above programme was recently conducted at Jaipur, Shillong, B alangir, 
Dharamshala and Srinagar.  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation

be done with the help of travel agencies and local businesses promoting their products and 
hotel-booking tickets at lowest prices. 
(Para 23) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
5.1 Projects developed under PRASHAD Scheme including creation of reception/facilitation

India Tourism offices located in the areas remain in touch with the State Governments to oversee

Recommendation/Observation 
6 The Committee desires that the Ministry should reinforce sustainable development in 
Indian tourism sector through the PRASHAD Scheme by transitioning to the use of renewable 
energy features such as photovoltaic electricity, waste water re -use and rainwater  recovery, 

9 
 
which not only will reduce the environmental impacts, but also generate benefits for local 
communities. 
(Para 25) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1 Ministry under its PRASHAD Scheme lays utmost importance to sustainability

Recommendation/Observation 
7 The Committee is of the view that approach to these destinations should be strengthened 
by proper roads, transport facilities, ticket booking facilities, lodging and other log istic support

ASSISTANCE TO CENTRAL AGENCIES SCHEME  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
8 The holistic development of tourism infrastructure at all tourist destinations through 
Central Financial Assistance to the States/ UTs may require convergence of resources, expertise

under the juris dictions of Central Agencies like ASI, Port Trusts in India, ITDC etc. and the

to devise mechanisms to build infrastructure with the assistance of state governments and other

(Para 31) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
8.1 The focus under the Assistance to Central Agencies Scheme is on the improvement/up -
gradation of existing products and developing new tourism products to the world standard, under 
the control of Central Agencies. State Governments participation is also ensured at the time of 
approval of the projects. 

10 
 
 
ADOPT A HERITAGE SCHEME (in collaboration with Ministry of Culture and ASI)  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
9 The Committee observes that the Ministry, with the assistance of business houses under 
the CSR, should build public amenities like public toilets, drinking water facility, ease of access 
for differently-abled citizens, standardized signage, surveillance system, night viewing facilities 
etc. in order to increase tourist footfall in the country. 
(Para 37) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
9.1 Adopt a Heritage project aims to encourage companies from public sector, private sector, 
trusts, NGOs, individuals and other stakeholders to become „Monument Mitras‟ and take up the 
responsibility of developing and upgrading the basic and advanced tourist amenities at heritage/ 
natural tourist sites as per their interest and viability in terms of a sustainable investment model 
under CSR. Public toilets, drinking water facility, ease of access for differently -abled citizens, 
standardized signage, surveillance system, nig ht viewing facilities etc. are covered under basic 
and advanced amenities proposed under the project. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
10 The Committee also observes that Souvenir shops selling miniatures of historical 
monuments are very popular among tourists in  foreign countries. However, these types of 
souvenir shops are very few in India and lack in marketing skills. The Committee would, 
therefore, recommend that the Government ought to take initiatives to help establish genuine 
outlets for the sale of miniature replicas of historical monuments near such monuments. 
(Para 38) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
10.1 Under Adopt a Heritage project, advanced amenities are planned as per the identified 
monument‟s tourist footfall and financial feasibility of proposed interventions. Provision of basic 
souvenir shop promoting local art and craftsmanship is covered under ad vanced amenities and 
may be implemented at the site upon adoption to provide a platform to local artisans/craftsmen to 
sell their product and support the local community.  
 
10.2 The Ministry of Tourism also under its „Swadesh Darshan Scheme‟ has sanctioned funds 
for development of Souvenir shops/Craft Haat etc. as per the guidelines for SD 2.0, the 
illustrative list of admissible components includes construction of craft Haats, Bazaars, souvenir 
shops, etc. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation

and festivals. Haats present a colourful picture where small artisans can nurture their crafts 
businesses. The Committee is of the opinion that development of haats shoul d be facilitated 
along with branding them as the go -to places on festive occasions, which will also lengthen the 

11 
 
tourist seasons, extend peak seasons or introduce a new season into a community. The 
Committee believes that such fairs and festivals not only serve to attract tourists but also

Reply of the Ministry 
11.1 Under Adopt a Heritage project, provision of basic souvenir shop promoting local art and 
craftsmanship is covered under advanced amenities and may be proposed at the site upon 
adoption. 
 
11.2 The Ministry of Tourism under its „Swadesh Darshan Scheme‟  has sanctioned funds for

Recommendation/Observation

Reply of the Ministry

12.2 The guidelines of SD2.0 scheme have a provision to fund both hard and soft interventions

12.3 Under Adopt a Heritage Project, 29 MoUs have been signed for development of basic

12.4 Out of 22, 11 Audio Guides have been completed in 4 languages (2 international) and 1

18 Tourism Police: The Committee notes that Safety and security of the tourists both 
domestic and foreign are Para  mount importance for projecting the country as a safe haven for 
tourism. There are occasional reports of incidents of misbehaviour, cheating, m alpractices etc. 
at various tourist places. This gives a bad publicity for that particular tourist destination and the 
country as a whole. Therefore, it is essential that the Government should take all the available 
measures to provide a safe environment f or the tourists. The Committee therefore recommends 
that in every tourist place, there should be a provision for tourism police, as a se parate wing of 
the police force to provide safety and security to the tourists. The Committee is fully aware that 
law and order is a part of the State subject. Therefore, the Ministry of Home Affairs should issue 
an advisory to all the State Governments to create tourism police in their State to provide safety 
and security to the tourists in tourist destinations. The Minist ry of Tourism should also take up 
the matter with all the State Governments for creation of separate tourism police in their 

14 
 
respective States. The Committee may be apprised of the action taken by the Ministry of Home 
Affairs and the Ministry of Tourism an d the feedback received from the State Governments in 
this regard. 
(Para 59) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
18.1 Safety and security aspects of tourists , is one of the most important issues, which the 
tourists take into account before planning a trip to a destination. Since the matter of “Police” and 
“Public Order” are the state subject under the VII Schedule of the Constitution of India, the 
matter regarding tourist safety and security is also taken up the State Govt./UT Adm inistration. 
The Ministry of Tourism has raised this issue with MHA on several occasions. 
 
18.2 MHA has already taken up the pilot project for providing tourist police at 25 tourist sites 
identified by the Ministry of Tourism. On the suggestions of the Ministry of Tourism, some of 
the State Governments have put the tourist police system in place. However, there remains 
variation at the policy and implementation level. 
 
18.3 The Ministry had also got a study conducted by IITTM, an autonomous institute under its 
control, to understand the requirement of tourist police and sensitizing the tourist police so 
created towards their needs.  
 
18.4 The Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) has prepa red a detailed 
report of developing the Scheme for Tourist Police, which may act as a template for the States 
and Union Territories for setting up the State/UT Tourist Police. The report is very 
comprehensive in its analysis and recommendations and once im plemented at the pan - India 
level, should be able to create an enabling framework for tourist safety. The contents of the 
report covers the relevant issues such as development of Standard Operating Procedures, setting 
up of Control Room Systems, defining t he role and responsibility of Tourist Police, uniform for 
Tourist Police personnel, training program, and scheme for incentivization for „ Tourist Police,‟ 
etc. 
 
18.5 Ministry of Tourism has been seeking support of the Ministry of Home Affairs for taking 
up the matter with the State Govt. to incorporate the issue of safety and security of tourists as one 
of the agenda points for the meetings to be held with DGPs of the State Govt./UT 
Administration.

its scheme for Development of Iconic Tourist Sites to harness the vast potential of Indian tourism 
sector and enhance India’s soft power. The Committee recommends that promoting the Scheme 
and taking it further with infrastructural, technological and skill development as well as 
branding and marketing to attract private investment will encourage tourism growth in 
unexplored areas of the country. 
(Para  43)

Further Recommendation/Observation:

REPORT 
 
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation on the recommendations/observations as contained in its T hree Hundred Twenty First 
Report on  „Issues related to S afety in Civil Aviation Sector‟ which was presented to both the 
Houses of Parliament on 31st March, 2022.  
 
2.  The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 13th September, 2022 in 
respect of all the observations/ recommendations contained in the Report. The replies hav e been 
categorized as follows:- 
 
Chapter-I: 
Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry: 
Paragraph Nos.: 19, 24 and 50

of the replies of the Ministry:

Total: 16 
 
Chapter-III:

accepted by the Committee: 
Paragraph Nos.: 8, 20, 31, 41, 43 and 55  
Total: 6 
 
Chapter-IV:

still awaited: 
Paragraph Nos.: Nil  
Total: Nil 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
Accident Investigation 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee notes that Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been 
allocated a meagre allocation of Rs. 1 crore, against its projected requirement of Rs. 4.40  crore 
in B.E. 2022 -23. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry may request the 
Ministry of Finance to provide AAIB with higher allocation at the R.E. 2022 -23 stage so as to 
enable it to perform its functions in the desired manner and contri bute towards improving the 
safety aspect of the civil aviation sector in India. 
 (Para 19) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has surplus funds available in 
comparison to its expenditure. However, the recommendation of the Committee has been noted 
for compliance. 
 
Passenger Safety 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee commends the extensive measures taken by the Ministry for the safety of 
flight passengers, airport staff, CISF and medical personnel, against the spread of the 
Coronavirus pandemic. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may ensure that best 
possible measures m ay continue to be employed across the airports in the country to keep a 
check on the rapid spread of any new Coronavirus variants in the future.  
(Para 24) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance. Apart from the 
steps taken for prevention of spread of Coronavirus, the guidelines/ instructions issued by the 
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare from time to time regarding prevention of COVID-19 are 
strictly followed at all the airports.  

3 
 
Scheduled Airlines Accident Rate 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee appreciates that India’s Scheduled Airlines Accident Rate is much below 
the world average rate and congratulates the Ministry of Civil Aviation and DGCA for ensuring 
such high safety standards. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may continue to give 
ample focus to ensure best global standards of aviation safety in the civil aviation sector in 
India. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may have similar focussed approach 
towards the safety of helicopter operations as well. 
 (Para 50) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1 DGCA has issued several publications like Rules, CARs, Circulars etc. for safe helicopter 
operations. However, the recommendation of the Committee has been noted. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

4 
 
CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
Directorate General of Civil Aviation 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee notes the mechanism existing at present in order to prevent aircraft 
accidents and thus ensure safety in civil aviation. The Committee recommends that the DGCA 
must regularly coordinate with AAI, various airport operators and airline operators and ensure 
the implementation of its specifications and guidelines regarding aviation safety. State -of-art 
technology may be installed and utilized for prevention of aircraft accidents/ malfunctioning. 
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may ensure that the budgetary allocation 
made to DGCA is sufficient to meet its requirements and it does not face any budgetary shortfall. 
Due focus may also be laid on ensuring that the human resource requirements of DGCA are met 
at all times so that it can effectively carry out the important mandate of ensuring safety in the 
civil aviation sector in the country. 
 (Para 7) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) conducts meetings with stakeholders/ 
airline/ airports operators as and when required for ensuring safe operations of aircraft. DGCA 
takes the input from the stakeholders, as and when required. The Governmen t has recently held 
meeting and sensitised the scheduled airlines to give utmost importance to safety of operations. 
Various steps have been taken which inter-alia include:              
(i) Scheduled Airlines have been asked to increase their engineering r elated capabilities at all 
base stations and transit stations.              
(ii) Additional special audits and spot checks have been ordered by DGCA.     
(iii) Airlines have been asked to take appropriate mitigation action and greater internal 
surveillance to ensure safety of air operations. 
  
1.2 Further, to ensure safety, DGCA implements the regulations and guidelines under 
Aircraft rules 1937 for regulating the airlines‟ operations. Further, these regulations are 

5 
 
amended/ revised by DGCA from time to time based upon the amendments in International Civil 
Aviation Organization ( ICAO) Annexes and based upon safe ty recommendations of Aircraft 
Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) / Directorate of Air safety, DGCA. Compl iance with 
these regulations is ensured during certification and during the regular surveillance of airline 
companies by DGCA. DGCA also conducts the Annual Surveillance Programme so as to meet 
the state obligations and to promote safe, orderly and efficie nt operation of aviation activities for 
safety oversight. 
  
1.3 Budgetary allocation to DGCA is always sufficient to meet its requirements. However, 
the observation of the Committee has been noted.  Further, adequate financial powers have also 
been delegated to DGCA. 
 
Safety of Air Transport Operations 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may review the efficiency of the mechanism 
presently in place for implementation of the processes recommended by ICAO for safety of air 
transport operations, from time to time so that these processes are implemented by the 
concerned organizations in letter and spirit. DGCA may hold periodical meetings with the 
stakeholders involved in the implementation of such processes and iron out any 
difficulties/bottlenecks being faced in following the processes laid down under the various ICAO 
Annexes. Concrete timelines may be prescribed by DGCA for effectuating any changes made by 
ICAO in its Annexes so as to ensure that best possible safety practic es are employed in the 
Indian civil aviation sector. 
 (Para 10) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 DGCA has a laid down process for ensuring compliance with the Standards and 
Recommended Practices (SARPs) laid down in the various ICAO safety -related Annexes. The 
process requires a time -bound action by DGCA wherein on receipt of the amendment to the 
Annexes, the same is reviewed and changes in regulations/ requirements are proposed. 
Thereafter, the draft regulation/ requirement after a stakeholder consultation process are 
finalised. Additionally, DGCA holds meetings with the stakeholders from time to time to discuss 

6 
 
and resolve issues in the implementation of the regulations based on the ICAO  Annexes and 
addresses any bottlenecks to ensure compliance and adherence to the Annexes. The Ministry of 
Civil Aviation regularly monitors the functionality of DGCA. The regulations proposed by 
DGCA are examined by the MoCA and whenever required suitable amendments are done in the 
Aircraft Act, 1934 or the Aircraft Rules, 1937. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee feels that the licensing of personnel including pilots, other Flight crew 
members, Aircraft Maintenance Engineers, Air Traffic Controlle rs etc. is a crucial process with 
a direct effect on the safety of the air transport operations in the country and thus utmost care 
must be taken to ensure that the licensing process for all such personnel is carried out strictly as 
per the established nor ms. The licences thus issued should be renewed periodically after 
carrying out necessary inspection and tests necessary for such approval. The Committee further 
recommends that training programmes may be arranged for different aviation sector personnel 
from time to time in order to keep them updated regarding the best safety practices in the 
aviation sector.  
(Para 11) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1 The rules for licensing of personnel including Pilots, other Flight Crew Members, 
Aircraft Maintenance Engineers, Air Traffic Controllers etc., are contained in the Aircraft Rules 
1937. To ensure that licensing process is carried out strictly as per the es tablished norms, 
„Training and Procedure Manual‟ is prepared for the guidance of officials performing these 
functions. This manual also contains the training requirements for all such officials for ensuring 
effective compliance of laid down norms. Procedur e for renewal of various license is also laid 
down in the same „Training and Procedure Manual‟ to ensure the compliance of above rules and 
regulations. Pilot license and ratings are issued and renewed only after ensuring strict compliance

Reply of the Ministry 
13.2 International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) requires the contracting States to 
establish and implement an effective safety oversight system taking into account eight critical 
elements (CEs). “Critical Elements” of the State‟s Safety Oversight System – ICAO has 
identified eight “Critical Elements” of the State‟s Safety Oversight System which require a 
contracting State to: 
1. Establish a comprehensive and effective aviation law.  
2. Establish operating regulations in conformity with the Standards and Recommended Practices 
(SARPs) contained in the Annexes to the Convention on International Civil Aviation. 
3. Establish State system and functions: Establish relevant authorities or government agencies, as 
appropriate, supported by sufficient and qualified personnel and provided with adequate financial 
resources for the management of safety.  
4. Establish techn ical personnel knowledge and training for technical personnel performing 
safety oversight functions.  
5. Establish technical guidance (including processes and procedures), tools (including facilities 
and equipment) and safety critical information for the technical personnel.  
6. Licensing, certification, authorization and approval obligation – Implement processes and 
procedures to ensure that the personnel and organizations performing an aviation activity meet 
the established requirements before they are al lowed to exercise the privileges of a licence,  
certificate, authorization and/or approval to conduct the relevant aviation activity.  
7. Surveillance obligation – Implement processes, such as inspections and audits, to proactively 
ensure that aviation licen ce, certificate, authorization and/or approval holders continue to meet 
the established requirements and function at the level of competency and safety required by the 
State to undertake an aviation -related activity for which they have been licensed, certi fied, 
authorized and/or approved to perform.  
8. Resolution of safety issues – Implement processes and procedures to resolve identified 
deficiencies impacting aviation safety, which may have been residing in the aviation system and 
have been detected by the regulatory authority or other appropriate bodies. In order to ensure that 
States are fulfilling their obligation of safety oversight under the Chicago Convention, ICAO, 
under its Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (USOAP), Continuous Monitoring 
Approach (CMA), conducts regular, mandatory, systematic and harmonized safety audits of all 

16 
 
the contracting States. The results of the audit are indicated in terms of the Effe ctive 
Implementation (EI) which is a  measure of the State‟s safety oversight capab ility, calculated for 
each critical element, each audit area or as an overall measure. The EI is expressed as a 
percentage. A high EI shows that the State‟s safety oversight capability is robust and meets the 
ICAO Standards while a low EI is indicative of poor safety oversight capability. The ICAO 
USOAP audit is carried out in the following eight areas: 
 
1. LEG (Primary Aviation Legislation and Specific Operating Regulation)  
2. ORG (Civil Aviation organization)  
3. PEL (Personnel Licensing)   
4. OPS (Aircraft Operations)  
5. AIR (Airworthiness of aircraft)  
6. Accident and Incident Investigation (AIG)  
7. Air Navigation Services (ANS)  
8. Aerodrome and Ground Aids (AGA)  
  
13.3 Based on the previous audits conducted by ICAO, the current EI of India is above the 
world average EI of 67.4%.  
  
13.4 Further, ICAO has planned an ICAO Coordinated Validation Mission (ICVM) of India in 
November, 2022. The scope of the ICVM would cover LE G (Legislation), ORG (Organisation), 
PEL (Personnel Licensing and Training), OPS (Aircraft Operations), AIR (Airworthiness of 
aircraft) and AGA (Aerodromes and Ground Aids) and will include an assessment and validation 
of the implementation of India‟s updated Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) addressing the findings 
from previous USOAP activities. DGCA has commenced preparation for the above ICVM. With 
the actions completed in particular related to the licensing of ATCOs by DGCA and the 
introduction of imposition of fines by DGCA, the score of India during the ICVM in November 
would raise the current EI.

FTO. We are expanding the capacity of Indian FTOs wit h a view to reduce the 
dependence on foreign FTOs. 
2. FTOs are regulated by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). The Aircraft 
Rules, 1937, require that the flying experience required for issue of private pilot and 
commercial pilot licenses shall be acquired only at DGCA-approved FTO. 

25 
 
3. DGCA follows a five -phase certification process for setting up a FTO to check all the 
laid down rules and regulations. The Directorate of Flying Training (DFT) at DGCA 
conducts scheduled annual inspections and unscheduled spot checks at FTOs. 
4. There are 35 DGCA -approved Flying Training Organisations (FTOs) in the 
country.  Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi ( IGRUA) at Amethi (UP) is under the 
administrative control of the Central Government. Eight FTOs are under State  
Governments and 26 are owned by the private sector. 
5. Airports Authority of India (AAI) has, on 25th September 2020, come up with a 
liberalised Flying Training Organisations (FTO s) policy wherein the concept of airport 
royalty (revenue share payment by FTOs  to AAI) has been abolished and land rentals 
have been significantly rationalised. 
6. AAI has issued award letters on 31st May 2021 and 29 October 2021 for nine FTOs to be 
established at five airports at Belagavi (Karnataka), Jalgaon (Maharashtra), Kalaburagi  
(Karnataka), Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh) and Lilabari (Assam). Soft launch of two 
FTOs at Kalaburagi was done on 15th August 2021 under the liberalised policy. Lilabari 
FTO, the First ever FTO in North-Eastern ( NE) States has been inaugurated on 12th 
April, 2022 and the remaining eight FTOs are targeted to be made operational by the end 
of 2022. 
6.2 Furthermore, in the second round 6 FTOs have been awarded at 5 Airports viz., 
Kishangarh, Hubballi, Kadapa, Bhavnagar and Salem Airports on 3rd June 2022. 
 
Further Recommendation/ Observation 
6.3 The Committee commends the steps taken to increase pilot training facilities. It 
would like to know the status of the operatio nalization of remaining 8 FTOs.  The 
Committee would also like to reiterate its recommendation to create provisions for creation 
of pilot training facilities with adequate space inside the airport may be incorporate d at the 
DPR stage itself. Further, the Committee may be apprised of the action taken to remove 
the deficiencies emerging out of audit of these schools recently.  
  

26 
 
CHAPTER-IV 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE FINAL 
REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY ARE STILL AWAITED 
 
 
-Nil -

CHAPTER-III 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
MINISTRY HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
Directorate General of Civil Aviation 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that there have been no helicopter accidents in the 
years 2020 and 2021, as compared to 2 accidents in 2018 and 3 in 2019. However, the

increasing steadily from 6 in 2018 to 7 each in 2019 & 2020 and 9 accidents in 2021. The 
Committee would like to know the reasons for the steady increase in the number of

accidents. 
(Para 1.6) 
Accident Investigation 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the AAIB is in the process of setting up its own

(Para 2.2) 
Air Traffic Controllers (ATCOs)

(Para 3.2) 

28 
 
Unmanned Aircraft Systems

(Para 4.3) 
Core Group on Safety 
The Committee notes the reply and would also like to know the comments of the Ministry

(Para 5.2)

REPORT 
The Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Culture on the 
recommendations/observations as contained in its Three Hundred and Eleventh Report on 
‘Creation of Regulatory Framework for Protection of Historical Sites and Monuments ’ which 
was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 3rd February, 2022. 
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 29th July, 13th October 
and 25 th October, 2022 in respect of all the recommendations/observations contained in the 
311th Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:— 
Chapter-I: 
Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry:  
Paragraph Nos.:  35A, 39, 41, 52 
Total:   4 
Chapter-II: 
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the replies of the Ministry: 
Paragraph Nos.:  14, 15, 16, 18, 33, 35 
Total:   6 
Chapter-III: 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have 
not been accepted by the Committee: 
Paragraph Nos.:  23, 34, 43, 47, 48, 48A, 50  
Total:   7 
Chapter-IV: 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the final replies of the 
Ministry are still awaited: 
Paragraph Nos.:   Nil  
Total:   Nil 
  

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
 
Efficacy of the existing Regulatory Framework to deal with the specific issue of 
encroachment of the Historical Sites and Monuments  
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee recommends that wherever possible, the Ministry/ASI should develop 
the area in the vicinity of the ancient monuments as green space with amenities for tourists 
since doing so will not only curb encroachment of that area but also bolster touri sm in the 
region.  
(Para 35A)  
Reply of Ministry  
1.1 The suggestion is noted for action, wherever possible.  
 
Review of existing provisions for grant of permission required for construction or 
repairs within the prohibited/ regulated areas of Centrally protected monuments  
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee fails to see why a person living in the Regulated Area of a CPM 
should be required to seek permission from the Competent Authority under the AMASR Rules 
for carrying out innocuous maintenance activities such as filling of cracks, whitewashing , 
replacement of windows etc. The Committee feels that such uncalled -for interference makes 
lives harder for people living nearby the monuments and could slowly cause feelings of 
anguish towards the monument itself. Given the large number of monuments acro ss the 
country and the limited budgetary resources available with the Government, it is pertinent 
that people residing near the monuments are encouraged to look after the monuments and 
protect them. Besides, placing such unnecessary curbs and implementing them is a wastage 
of limited Government resources and turns the focus away from where it should be - actually 
protecting and preserving the monument itself. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
the Ministry may undertake a thorough review of the AMASR  Act and Rules and omit any 
provisions that provide for seeking permissions for minor works where the same is not 
actually needed and streamline the process for applying for permission in case where the 
same is actually needed. Steps may urgently be taken to make it possible for the entire 
process for seeking permission for construction activities in prohibited and regulated areas, 
to be completed online so as to not cause any hassle to bona fide residents living near the 
monuments.  

3 
 
(Para 39)  
Reply of Ministry  
2.1 Recommendation is noted for action as appropriate. 
 
Evolving ways for participation of municipalities and village panchayats in the process 
of protection of regional Historical Sites and Monuments 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. Given the large number of historical monuments and sites located across the country, 
many of which are not under any sort of protection from the Central/State Governments, the 
Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 5.7.23 of its 294 th Report on the 
subject ‘Development and Conservation of Museums and Archaeological sites - Challenges 
and Opportunities ’ and recommends that the Ministry should find ways to institutionally 
integrate municipalities and village panchayats in the process of protection of historical  
monuments and sites across the country and if needed, create a dedicated body to implement 
the regulatory framework for the same.  
(Para 41)  
Reply of Ministry  
3.1 Noted for action as appropriate. 
 
Miscellaneous  
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee recommends that ASI may frame Disaster Management Plan for the 
monuments at the earliest since disasters can cause irreversible damage to our invaluable 
historical monuments and sites and sincere efforts have to be made to have plans in place  to 
minimize the damage caused due to such adversities.  
(Para 52)  
Reply of Ministry  
4.1 Noted for compliance.  
  

4 
 
CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. In light of the observations made by various experts on the subject and the lack of any 
specific reasoning behind the limit of 100 metres and 300 metres around the CPMs as 
prohibited and regulated areas, the Committee is of the strong view that the Ministry must 
undertake a holistic, in -depth review of the restrictions imposed by the AMASR Act on 
construction activities near the CPMs since it does not seem logica l to have restrictions on a 
uniform amount of area across the highly diverse types of monuments under the protection of 
the Central Government. The Committee takes serious notice of the observation made by one 
of the experts that the 2010 amendment was bro ught about without any inputs from the ASI 
and recommends that the review of the existing legislation should be carried out in 
consultation with existing and former senior officials of ASI, and other subject experts. The 
Committee recommends that the area to be deemed as prohibited and regulated area should 
not be set in stone for all the monuments and should instead be decided on a case -to-case 
basis, with due consideration to the individual requirements of the monument/site. There is 
no denying the fact t hat there needs to be a mechanism for keeping a check on the 
construction activities in the vicinity of a historical monument but utmost care must be taken 
to ensure that doing so causes least possible disruption in the lives of people who have had 
been li ving in harmony with the monuments since decades, duly factoring in the specific 
requirements for such checks given the unique nature of the individual historical monuments. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should urgently work towards creating a  
regulatory framework that has provisions for the least possible restrictions on construction 
activities in a manner suitable to the specific requirements for individual monuments while 
ensuring that no structural or visual damage is caused to the monument  by any construction 
activities and does not unnecessarily impinge on the rights of people living nearby the 
monuments. 
(Para 14)  
 Reply of Ministry  
1.1 The issue has been taken into consideration under proposed amendment in 
consultation with other experts also. 
 
 
 

5 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee agrees with the concerns raised by one of the experts regarding the 
prohibitions imposed by the AMASR (Amendment) Act, 2010 on appointment of any person 
who has held any post with the ASI or the Ministry of Culture, as the Chairman or member of 
the NMA. The Committee feels that having the services of personnel who have had actual 
field experience working for the preservation and protection of the historical monuments and 
sites, could help NMA fulf ill its mandate in a more effective manner but many people with 
such experience would be those who have had worked with the ASI or Ministry of Culture 
and thus would be deemed ineligible to be appointed as the Chairman or member of the NMA 
as per the exist ing provisions of the AMASR Act. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry may revisit the rationale behind the restrictions imposed by Section 20F(3) of the 
AMASR (Amendment and Validation) Act, 2010 and consider the pros and cons behind 
imposing such a restriction on the appointment of Chairman and members of the NMA. 
Further, the Committee notes that the NMA has also been given the responsibility of 
classification and gradation of monuments in consultation with ASI. The Committee 
recommends that NMA may complete the classification and gradation exercise at the earliest. 
The Committee feels that doing so, alongwith preparation of heritage byelaws for all CPMs, 
would permit the Ministry to come up with provisions for restrictions best suited for each 
monument instead of blanket bans that fail to serve the intended purpose. 
(Para 15)  
Reply of Ministry  
2.1 The issue has been taken into consideration under proposed amendment. Actions are 
also initiated for enabling the work of preparation of Heritage Bye-laws at faster rate.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may introduce the concept of 
Transferable Development Rights to enable people having properties in the vicinity of the 
monuments to monetize their properties. The Committee feels that this would act as a 
deterrent to encroachment of monuments, especially in case the monument is located in a 
congested urban area.  
(Para 16) 
Reply of Ministry  
3.1 Transfer of Development rights is not within the jurisdiction of MoC. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee takes note of the extensive list of suggestions made by the expert 
regarding the new Rules/ Regulations/ Policies/ Legislation/ Amendments that can be 

6 
 
introduced in order to ensure better protection of the Historical Sites and Monuments. The 
Committee reiterates its recommendation made in Para 14 of this Report and recommends 
that the Ministry may thoroughly examine the above -mentioned suggestions made by the 
expert while undertaking the review of the AMASR Act. The Ministry must ensure that t he 
review of the existing legislation may factor in feedback from experts in the field of 
conservation, preservation, archaeology, law as well as all the stakeholders who are 
impacted by the AMASR Act.  
(Para 18)  
Reply of Ministry  
4.1 Stakeholder consultations w ere done while working on AMASR Amendment and  
their views have been suitably taken into consideration.  
 
Efficacy of the existing Regulatory Framework to deal with the specific issue of 
encroachment of the Historical Sites and Monuments  
Recommendation/Observation 
5. The Committee notes the existing provisions in place in order to deal with the issue of 
encroachment of Centrally Protected Monuments and the loopholes/ gaps/ glitches pointed 
out by various experts. The Committee agrees with the suggestion made by one of the experts 
that amendments are required in order to ensure that encroachment of monuments are 
removed as quick as possible in fast track courts. The Committee feels that doing so can 
permit the encroachment to be removed befo re any permanent structure is constructed in the 
vicinity of the monument, thus preventing any sort of possible damages to the monument.  
(Para 33)  
Reply of Ministry  
5.1 The issue of removal of encroachments is suitably being addressed in the proposed 
amendment.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may undertake a thorough review of the 
AMASR Act as well as the AMASR Rules in terms of the powers available with ASI to tackle 
the issue of encroachment of monuments, keeping in view the various loopholes and gap s 
pointed out by legal experts. The Committee feels that the Ministry should incorporate 
provisions similar to those relating to encroachment in the Indian Forest Act, 1927, in the 
AMASR Act in order to empower ASI to effectively deal with the issue of enc roachment of 
monuments. The Committee further recommends that the AMASR Act should grant power to 
ASI to seal the site of illegal construction till the time the demolition can be done, so that any 
delay in the same does not cause any further damage to the monument and there is no 

7 
 
incentive for encroachers to undertake any illegal construction near the monument. The 
Ministry should request the Ministry of Finance to provide it with separate budget to carry 
out the demolition of unauthorized constructions tha t have taken place in the vicinity of 
Centrally Protected Monuments.  
(Para 35)  
Reply of Ministry  
6.1 The issue of removal of encroachments is suitably being addressed in the proposed 
amendment. As per the AMASR Rules, 1959 the demolition of unauthorised constructions is 
to be carried out at the cost of defaulter. 
 
 
 
  

8 
 
CHAPTER-III 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF 
THE MINISTRY HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
Suggestions for creation of Regulatory Framework for protection of Historical 
Monuments presently not under the protection of both Central and State Governments 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry may consider coming up 
with a legislation to amend the Constitution adding ―ancient and historical monuments 
other than those declared to be of national importance to the Concurrent List, in order to 
permit the Central Government to enforce at least some set of provisions for the basic 
protection and conservation of archaeological monuments and sites which are presently not 
under any sort of protection by Central and State Governments. A separate Herita ge 
Commission may thereafter be established to look after such monuments. Since a 
Constitutional amendment is a time -taking process, the Committee recommends that in the 
meanwhile, the Ministry may come up with policy guidelines which can be adopted by the  
State Governments across the country for looking after neglected archaeological sites and 
monuments. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may request for certain 
budgetary allocation to allow ASI to carry out urgent conservation measures at such 
miscellaneous monuments, possibly in coordination with concerned State Archaeology 
Departments.  
(Para 23)  
Reply of Ministry  
1.1 ASI has provisions to undertake conservation measures at ancient monuments which 
are not of national importance. Certain budgetary allocation is also made for this purpose.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
1.2 The reply furnished by the Ministry does not  state whether it has taken any 
action to frame policy guidelines which can be adopted by the State Governments across 
the country for looking after neglected archaeological sites and monuments . The 
Committee desires to be informed whether the Ministry has taken any action in this 
regard. Further, the Committee may be apprised regarding the budgetary allocation 
made and u tilized by ASI for monuments which are not of national importance and 
what are the guidelines/ rules in place for taking up such conservation works. 
 
 

9 
 
Efficacy of the existing Regulatory Framework to deal with the specific issue of 
encroachment of the Historical Sites and Monuments  
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee is concerned to note that the final notification of declaration of an 
ancient/historical monument/site/remains as of national importance, is not published by ASI 
in most cases. The Committee recommends that a time-bound limit may be prescribed for ASI 
to publish the final notification, alongwith the site map, for monuments under its protection 
since the purpose of the same is to verify the physical structure and to determine the 
portion/part/extent of the monument that is required to be within the protected limits.  
(Para 34)  
Reply of Ministry  
2.1 Declaring any monument as of national importance and publication final notification 
therefor involve consultation with State Government,  Stakeholder, Management Committee 
or sometimes land owners. Such formalities may consume much time -case to case basis and 
are beyond the jurisdiction of ASI/MoC Sometimes, legal issue may crop up. As such it 
appears not feasible to specify a fix time limit to publish final notification. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
2.2 The Committee notes that the declaration of any monument to be of national 
importance and publication of final notification therefor is a time -consuming process 
since it involves consultation with State Government, Stakeholder, Management 
Committee or sometimes land owners.  However, the more extensive the tasks, the 
greater is the need for setting time limits.  The Committee feels that having a clear time -
limit for publication of the final notification is required to mitigate the present situation 
wherein the final notification of declaration of an  ancient/historical 
monument/site/remains as of national importance, is not published  at all  by ASI in 
many cases, even after passage of very long time  since publication of preliminary 
notification. The Committee  strongly recommends that t he Ministry may prescribe  a 
well-defined time-bound limit for ASI to publish the final notification  of declaration of 
an ancient/historical monuments/site/remains as of national importance , along with the 
site map, for monuments under its protection.  While deciding upon the time -limit to be 
fixed for this purpose, the Ministry may duly factor in the time-consuming nature of the 
process for publication of final notification. 
 
Preparation of monument -specific conservation plan and bye -laws for all Centrally 
Protected Monuments across the country 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee opines that the Ministry/ASI/NMA should carry out an exercise to 
prepare monument -specific conservation plans and heritage bye -laws for all Centrally 

10 
 
Protected Monuments across the country, since there cannot be a uniform plan for all the 
monuments and the unique conservation requirements of each monument can only be 
reflected through dedicated conservation plan for each monument. Such an exercise would  
undoubtedly require sufficient manpower and resources. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry should ensure that swift action is taken to ensure that ASI is adequately staffed at all 
times and staffing requirements should be anticipated well in advanc e since recruitment of 
quality personnel is often a time-taking exercise. The Committee further recommends that the 
Ministry should formulate the budgetary requirements for creation of dedicated conservation 
plans for all CPMs and request the Ministry of F inance to grant the same as a special one -
time grant.  
(Para 43)  
Reply of Ministry  
 
3.1 For the conservation of monuments an annual conservation programme is prepared by 
the Circles concerned as per the requirement and priority of the monuments/ sites. B ased on 
the approved annual conservation programme, conservation works are carried out. In  
addition, Site Management Plans (SMPs) for select WH monuments have also been prepared 
by ASI. 
3.2 Promotions held in ASI during 2021 and 2022 (till date) are attac hed at Annexure-I. 
Further, plan for filling up vacant posts and promotion for upcomi ng years are also given at 
Annexure-II. 
3.3 Annual budget for the conservation of monuments is provided by the Ministry of 
Culture to the Archaeological Survey of India. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
3.4 The Committee observes that the annual conservation programme prepared by 
the Circles concerned is as per the requirement and priority of the monuments/ sites. 
The Committee, however, feels that the requirements and priority of conservation work 
at the monuments/ sites cannot be effectively gauged unless monument -specific 
conservation plans are prepared for all monuments in the respective circles  and 
therefore, recommends that provisions may be introduced to prepare m onument-
specific conservation plans so as to ensure suitable state of conservation for all Centrally 
Protected Monuments. 
 
3.5 The Committee notes the details furnished by the Ministry regarding the status 
of direct recruitment to the various posts in ASI and is concerned to note  that more  
than 2,000 vacancies exist at various posts in ASI at present. In this regard, the 
Committee may be apprised whether ASI factors in the time taken by the recruiting 
agencies to complete the recruitment process, while repo rting its vacancies to such 
agencies. Given the evident scarcity of manpower available with ASI in view of the large 
number of Centrally Protected Monuments across the country, anticipating the delays 
in the process of recruitment while reporting vacancies / upcoming vacancies, is of 

11 
 
crucial importance. Effective steps, therefore, must be taken in this regard to ensure 
that ASI is adequately staffed at all times  and recruitment process is put in motion well 
in advance for the same,  so as to ensure sufficient  protection and preservation of our 
tangible cultural heritage. 
 
Security policy for all Centrally Protected Monuments 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may carry out an exercise to figure out 
the requirements for security infrastructure as well as for posting security personnel at each 
monument. The data thus obtained may be used to frame a comprehensive security  policy for 
all the Centrally Protected Monuments so as to ensure a satisfactory level of protection of 
CPMs across the country. The Committee acknowledges the budgetary constraints faced by 
the Ministry and recommends that the Ministry may request the Min istry of Finance to 
provide sufficient budget to allow it to post security personnel at all CPMs across the 
country. Outsourcing should be done to appoint staff for security of the monuments and 
guides should be trained and they should also be made respons ible for taking care of the 
property.  
(Para 47) 
Reply of Ministry  
4.1 Noted for action as appropriate. Action has to be taken up by the Ministry of Culture.  
 
4.2 Guides- Guide matter is handled by the Ministry of Tourism ( MoT). Therefore, MoT 
may take suitable action.   
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
4.3 The Committee desires to be apprised whether the Ministry of Culture has taken 
any action to seek sufficient budget from the Ministry of Finance to allow it to post 
security personnel  at all Centrally Protected Monuments across the country  and 
whether any action has been taken on the issue of training of guides by the Ministry of 
Tourism. Further, t he Committee is of the view that given the extensive knowledge  
possessed by ASI regarding Centrally Protected Monuments across the country, having 
a suitable mechanism for coordination between ASI and Ministry of Tourism will help 
improve the training standards of Tourist Guides working at such sites.  Sensitization 
programmes for guides may also be carried out in coordination with the Ministry of 
Tourism to encourage them to look after the Centrally Protected Monuments while 
guiding the tourists. 
 
 

12 
 
Improving the mechanism for coordination between ASI and State Government 
Departments  
Recommendation/Observation 
5. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may issue guidelines to the State 
Government Departments concerned to approach the ASI in cases where the State protected 
Monuments require the technical expertise available with ASI for better protection and 
preservation of State -protected monuments. The Committee further recommends that the 
regional offices of ASI should proactively review the status of protection and preservation of 
State-protected monuments and in case gross neglec t in the same is observed, the matter 
should be taken up with the State Government Department concerned. The Committee feels 
that a mechanism should be put in place to enable periodic exchange of information about 
the developmental/ conservation/ protection measures taken by ASI and State Departments.  
(Para 48)  
Reply of Ministry  
 
5.1 The point is noted for compliance. However,  wherever necessary, ASI provides 
technical expertise and guidance to the State Governments for undertaking conservation of 
State-protected and unprotected monuments.  In addition, if requested by the State 
Governments, ASI also takes up conservation of State Protected / Unprotected monuments.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
5.2 The Committee desires to be apprised of the procedure under which ASI 
provides technical expertise and guidance to the State Governments and the details of 
such instances in the last 3 years.  
 
Miscellaneous  
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee recommends that the Ministry/ASI, in coordination with the State 
Government Archaeology/Culture Department concerned, should take up the restoration of 
historical/ religious sites having heritage value and architectural and cultural significa nce 
such as temples which are more than 100 years old and which have been converted into 
mixed-use buildings such as residential property or government building, to their original 
shape. A time -bound implementation programme should be made for the same and  
accountability of officials working on these projects should be fixed so that the restoration 
works are completed on time and in a satisfactory manner. The Ministry may approach the 
Ministry of Finance to allocate separate budget for this purpose. The Com mittee further 
recommends that it should be mandated that the management bodies for religious sites shall 
get periodically audited regarding the state of conservation, safety and security of the 
monuments and the amount of funds/donations received and spen t, so as to ensure that such 

13 
 
funds are not diverted for unrelated purposes.  
(Para 48A)  
Reply of Ministry  
 
6.1 ASI provides technical  expertise and guidance to the State Governments to take up 
the restoration of historical/ religious sites having heritage value and architectural and 
cultural significance. 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
6.2 The Committee reiterates its recommendation made under  ‘Further 
Recommendation/Observation’ at para 5.2 of Chapter III of this Report. 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry is working on a much -needed 
amendment of the AMASR Act,  1958. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may 
incorporate the recommendations made by the Committee in this Report and factors in 
feedback from experts and stakeholders in the amendment of the AMASR Act.  
(Para 50) 
Reply of Ministry  
 
7.1 The final Draft Cabinet Note and Bill has been prepared after considering comments 
received from various State Governments, consultation with heritage experts and inter 
ministerial consultation. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
7.2 The Committee notes that the reply furnished by the Ministry does not make any 
mention of the recommendations made by the Committee in its 311 th Report having 
been incorporated in the final Draft Cabinet Note and Bill . The Committee desires to be 
apprised in this regard.

Assessment of Demands for Grants (2022-23) of the Ministry 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee notes that while the projected  demand of the Ministry for 2022 -23 was 
Rs. 11,183.10 crores, an allocation of Rs. 10,667.00 [Rs. 10,590.54 (Revenue) + Rs. 76.46 
(Capital)] crores has been made, which indicates a shortfall of Rs. 516.10 crores. It also noted 
that shortfall is mainly on a ccount of decreased allocations for AIAHL and RCS, while budget 
for projects and programmes have been adjusted as per priority of execution. The Committee is 
of the opinion that the decreased allocation for AIAHL is justified, in view of the fact that the 
process of disinvestment of Air India is almost complete, however, not agreeing to the 
projections for the RCS by a staggering amount of Rs. 101.28 crores is cause of concern. The 
Committee feels that the RCS Scheme, which has given a big boost to affordab le connectivity, 
should have been encouraged by the Government, through sufficient budgetary support. A 
curtailment of funds at this stage may hamper the smooth development of this important scheme. 
The Committee is aware that the Civil Aviation sector is reeling under stress and different 
players have also suffered massive losses due to COVID -19 pandemic and need a helping hand 
from the Government at this critical juncture, yet the Ministry has not been allocated the desired 
projected amount for B.E. 2022 -23. The Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry‟s 
request for additional funds for all schemes/ heads, including RCS scheme at the R.E. 2022 -23 
stage may be favourably considered by the Ministry of Finance. 
(Para 8) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 The observations of the Committee have been noted. Regarding the budgetary provision 
under RCS Scheme, it is submitted that the budget allocation under the scheme  at BE 2022 -23 
has been made considering the status of the progress of the projects  covered under R CS. The 
status of the UDAN airport  is reviewed from time to time and if required, the Ministry will take 
up the matter with MoF for enhanced budget at RE stage in FY 2022-23.

compared to projected amount for 2022 -23 for DGCA by Rs. 37.08 crores, BCAS by Rs. 22.62 
crores and National Aviation University by Rs. 8.60 crores. There has also been a decrease in 
B.E. 2022-23 (Capital) for BCAS by Rs. 13.31 crores and AAIB by Rs. 3.40 crore, where less 
than one-fourth of the projected amount of Rs. 4.40 crores has been allocated. The Committee

(Para 9)

2.1 The recommendations of th e Committee for allocation of additional funds  for DGCA,

Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee notes that over the last five years, the percentage of allocated budget at 
R.E. stage, on projected demand has varied from 56.36%, 59.19% and 34.78%. While in 2020 -
21, it was substantially raised to 84% of the projected demand. In 2021 -22, the Ministry was 
allocated Rs. 72,652 crores, which was more than the projected demand of Rs. 67,844.62 crores 
and the higher allocation was on ac count of “Disinvestment of Air India Limited‟. For this year 
also, 86.80% of the total allocation of Rs. 10,667.00 crores was for AIAHL (SPV), leaving only a 
meager portion of 13.2% amounting to Rs. 1407.09 crores for allocation to the rest of the heads. 
The Committee is of the opinion that such a low allocation over the years will seriously affect the 
growth of the Civil Aviation sector, which is already suffering from a downturn caused by 
COVID-19 pandemic. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the issue of low allocation 
may be taken up with the Ministry of Finance at R.E. stage and need for higher allocations may 
be stressed upon. 
(Para 12)
